heuristics.rule: 2-year cohabitation threshold for statutory property-division rights
heuristics.condition: When an unmarried couple in British Columbia has lived together in a marriage-like relationship for at least two years
heuristics.action: The same property-division rights that apply to married couples under BC's Family Law Act apply to the unmarried couple
heuristics.because: BC's Family Law Act explicitly extends married-couple property-division rights to unmarried couples who meet the 2-year threshold; below two years, no statutory property-division right exists by default
heuristics.regulatory_basis: BC Family Law Act — 2-year marriage-like relationship threshold

heuristics.rule: Child's physical, emotional, and psychological safety, security, and well-being must receive primary consideration — not equal weighting — in any parenting order determination
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian court is determining decision-making responsibility or parenting time under a parenting order
heuristics.action: Court must give primary consideration to the child's physical, emotional, and psychological safety, security, and well-being before weighing all other factors
heuristics.because: Divorce Act s.16(2) statutorily mandates this priority ordering — safety/security/well-being is not one factor among equals but the factor the court is legally required to prioritize
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Divorce Act s.16(2)

heuristics.rule: 12-month separation before divorce finalization
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian spouse seeks divorce on the ground of separation
heuristics.action: The application may be filed before 12 months elapse, but the divorce cannot be granted until a full 12 months of separation has passed
heuristics.because: The Divorce Act requires that spouses have separated and lived apart for at least one year before a separation-based divorce can be finalized
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Department of Justice Canada — Divorce Act fact sheet, separation period requirement

heuristics.rule: Married spouses in Ontario must split property acquired during marriage equally via an equalization payment
heuristics.condition: When a marriage ends for any reason in Ontario
heuristics.action: Calculate each spouse's net family property (property value at separation minus debts and excluded property, minus pre-marriage property value minus pre-marriage debts); the spouse with the larger net family property pays half the difference to the other
heuristics.because: Ontario law requires equalization of net family property upon marriage breakdown — this is not a physical 50/50 asset split but a payment equalizing the financial gain each spouse made during the marriage
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Government of Ontario (ontario.ca) — dividing property when marriage or common-law relationship ends

heuristics.rule: California courts evaluate custody using the six enumerated factors under California Family Code §3011
heuristics.condition: When a California court is determining child custody
heuristics.action: Judge must weigh: (1) age and health of the child, (2) emotional ties between parents and child, (3) child's ties to school, home, and community, (4) ability of each parent to care for the child, (5) any history of family violence, (6) any regular and ongoing substance abuse by either parent
heuristics.because: These are the statutory factors California Family Code §3011 requires courts to apply under the 'best interests of the child' standard
heuristics.regulatory_basis: California Family Code §3011

heuristics.rule: California 6-month state residency requirement for divorce filing
heuristics.condition: When a spouse wishes to file for divorce in California...
heuristics.action: At least one spouse must have lived in California for the last 6 months before filing
heuristics.because: California courts require established residency to assert jurisdiction over a dissolution of marriage proceeding
heuristics.regulatory_basis: California Courts Self-Help Center (Judicial Branch of California), selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/divorce-california

heuristics.rule: In community property states, all assets acquired during the marriage are owned equally 50/50 by both spouses regardless of whose name appears on the asset or who earned the income.
heuristics.condition: When a couple divorces and is domiciled in Arizona, California, Idaho, Louisiana, Nevada, New Mexico, Texas, Washington, or Wisconsin...
heuristics.action: Apply a mechanical 50/50 split to all marital property, income, and debt acquired during the marriage.
heuristics.because: Community property law treats both spouses as equal co-owners of everything acquired during the marriage by operation of law, not by judicial discretion.
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Cornell Law School LII — Wex: community_property

heuristics.rule: Pre-relationship property stays separate; property acquired during the relationship is shared
heuristics.condition: When the 2-year threshold is met and the couple separates
heuristics.action: Property brought into the relationship by either partner remains that partner's separate property; property acquired together during the relationship is divided
heuristics.because: BC's Family Law Act specifies that common-law partners 'will generally share any property they acquire during the course of their relationship — but not property brought into the relationship'
heuristics.regulatory_basis: BC Family Law Act — family property definition for common-law couples

heuristics.rule: Parenting orders are determined exclusively on the best interests of the child — not on which parent 'wins' custody as a concept
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian court is assigning decision-making responsibility and parenting time
heuristics.action: Court must frame its determination around best interests of the child, not around a custody-win framework for either parent
heuristics.because: The Divorce Act structures the entire parenting order determination around the best interests standard, displacing adversarial custody framing
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Divorce Act (parenting order provisions)

heuristics.rule: At least one spouse must have resided in a Canadian province or territory for at least one year before applying
heuristics.condition: When either spouse files for divorce under the federal Divorce Act
heuristics.action: Confirm that at least one spouse meets the one-year provincial/territorial residency requirement before filing
heuristics.because: If neither spouse meets the residency requirement, divorce under the federal Divorce Act is unavailable
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Department of Justice Canada — Divorce Act fact sheet, residency requirement

heuristics.rule: The matrimonial home cannot have its pre-marriage, gift, or inheritance value excluded from the equalization calculation
heuristics.condition: When calculating net family property and one spouse owned the family home before marriage, or received it as a gift or inheritance
heuristics.action: Include the full value of the family home in the equalization calculation — do not deduct the pre-marriage value, gift value, or inheritance value as an exclusion
heuristics.because: Ontario law treats the family home specially: the standard exclusions for pre-marriage property, gifts, and inheritances explicitly do not apply to the matrimonial home
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Government of Ontario (ontario.ca) — dividing property when marriage or common-law relationship ends

heuristics.rule: Documented family violence is an explicit statutory aggravating factor in California custody determinations
heuristics.condition: When any history of family violence exists in a custody case
heuristics.action: Court must weigh family violence history as a named factor under §3011 — it is not discretionary to consider or ignore
heuristics.because: California Family Code §3011 explicitly enumerates family violence as one of the six determinative factors, meaning it directly affects custody outcome, not merely background context
heuristics.regulatory_basis: California Family Code §3011

heuristics.rule: California 3-month county residency requirement for divorce filing
heuristics.condition: When a spouse wishes to file for divorce in a specific California county...
heuristics.action: At least one spouse must have resided in that specific California county for the last 3 months before filing
heuristics.because: California courts require county-level residency to determine the proper local court venue for filing
heuristics.regulatory_basis: California Courts Self-Help Center (Judicial Branch of California), selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/divorce-california

heuristics.rule: Property owned before the marriage, or received individually as a gift or inheritance during the marriage, is classified as separate property and excluded from community property division.
heuristics.condition: When identifying which assets are subject to the 50/50 community property split...
heuristics.action: Exclude pre-marital property and individually received gifts or inheritances from the marital estate subject to division.
heuristics.because: The community property regime only attaches to assets acquired during the marriage; separately held property retains its individual character.
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Cornell Law School LII — Wex: community_property

heuristics.rule: Written agreement can opt out of default statutory property-division rules
heuristics.condition: When an unmarried couple in BC does not want the Family Law Act's default property-division rules to apply
heuristics.action: The couple must execute a written agreement contracting out of the statutory default rules
heuristics.because: BC's Family Law Act permits couples to contract out entirely via a written agreement; without such an agreement, the statutory defaults apply automatically once the 2-year threshold is met
heuristics.regulatory_basis: BC Family Law Act — opt-out via written agreement

heuristics.rule: The factor list under the Divorce Act is explicitly non-exhaustive
heuristics.condition: When a court is applying the best interests of the child standard
heuristics.action: Court may consider case-specific factors not enumerated in the statutory list
heuristics.because: The Act explicitly designates the listed factors as non-exhaustive, preserving judicial discretion to weigh circumstances unique to the case
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Divorce Act (best interests factor provisions)

heuristics.rule: No-fault separation ground is the dominant path; fault-based grounds (cruelty, adultery) require proof and are rarely pursued
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian spouse is choosing which ground to cite for divorce
heuristics.action: Default to the separation ground unless there is a specific legal reason to pursue cruelty or adultery, as those require evidentiary proof
heuristics.because: The existence of the one-year no-fault separation path makes fault-based grounds procedurally burdensome without commensurate benefit in the vast majority of cases
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Department of Justice Canada — Divorce Act fact sheet, three grounds for divorce

heuristics.rule: A court claim for equalization must be brought within 6 years from separation OR 2 years from finalized divorce, whichever comes first
heuristics.condition: When a married spouse in Ontario intends to pursue a court claim for the equalization amount
heuristics.action: File the court claim before the earlier of: 6 years from the date of separation, or 2 years from the date the divorce is finalized
heuristics.because: Missing the limitation period bars the court claim for equalization entirely
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Government of Ontario (ontario.ca) — dividing property when marriage or common-law relationship ends

heuristics.rule: Regular and ongoing substance abuse by either parent is an explicit statutory aggravating factor in California custody determinations
heuristics.condition: When either parent has a pattern of regular and ongoing substance abuse
heuristics.action: Court must weigh this as a named factor under §3011; the substance abuse must be 'regular and ongoing' — isolated or historical use does not meet the statutory language
heuristics.because: California Family Code §3011 specifies 'regular and ongoing' as the threshold qualifier — the standard is not any substance use but a continuing pattern
heuristics.regulatory_basis: California Family Code §3011

heuristics.rule: Mandatory wait when neither spouse meets California residency requirement
heuristics.condition: When neither spouse has met the 6-month state and 3-month county residency requirements...
heuristics.action: Both spouses must generally wait until the residency requirement is met before filing in California
heuristics.because: Filing eligibility is contingent on satisfying both residency thresholds; no exception or waiver is stated in the official guidance
heuristics.regulatory_basis: California Courts Self-Help Center (Judicial Branch of California), selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/divorce-california

heuristics.rule: In Alaska, community property treatment is opt-in — it applies only if the couple has elected it by agreement.
heuristics.condition: When a couple divorcing in Alaska seeks to determine which property regime governs their marital assets...
heuristics.action: First determine whether the couple entered a community property agreement; if no agreement exists, community property rules do not apply by default.
heuristics.because: Alaska does not impose community property by operation of law; it requires an affirmative election by the spouses.
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Cornell Law School LII — Wex: community_property

heuristics.rule: Province is a required diagnostic fact for any Canadian unmarried couple considering separation and property division
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian user who is unmarried asks what happens to shared property if they leave a relationship
heuristics.action: Identify the province before answering; BC and Ontario have materially different rules and a generic 'Canada' answer is not valid
heuristics.because: BC grants automatic property-division rights after 2 years of cohabitation; Ontario does not grant automatic property division to common-law couples regardless of duration — province determines whether statutory rights exist at all
heuristics.regulatory_basis: BC Family Law Act vs. Ontario family law framework (province-variance principle)

heuristics.rule: Use 'parenting arrangements' terminology, not 'custody and access', for post-divorce child arrangements
heuristics.condition: When describing where children will live and how decisions about them are made in any Canadian divorce proceeding on or after March 1, 2021
heuristics.action: Apply the term 'parenting arrangements' as defined under the amended Divorce Act
heuristics.because: The Divorce Act was amended effective March 1, 2021 to replace 'custody and access' with 'parenting arrangements', reflecting a statutory reframing of child-related decisions
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Department of Justice Canada — Divorce Act fact sheet, terminology shift effective March 1, 2021

heuristics.rule: Common-law couples in Ontario have no automatic property division rights regardless of relationship duration
heuristics.condition: When a common-law couple in Ontario separates, regardless of how long they lived together
heuristics.action: Each partner retains only what they individually purchased — no equalization payment or automatic division applies
heuristics.because: Ontario law does not grant common-law partners automatic property-division rights; there is no duration threshold (unlike BC) that triggers such rights
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Government of Ontario (ontario.ca) — dividing property when marriage or common-law relationship ends

heuristics.rule: The 'best interests of the child' standard is used across all US states for custody, but specific enumerated factors vary by state
heuristics.condition: When a custody determination is made in any US state
heuristics.action: Apply the best interests standard using that state's specific enumerated factors — do not assume California's six factors apply universally across states
heuristics.because: The source explicitly states the standard is universal across US states but 'the specific enumerated factors vary by state'
heuristics.regulatory_basis: California Family Code §3011 (California implementation); standard applied in all US states with state-specific factor variations

heuristics.rule: No-fault filing: spousal agreement not required
heuristics.condition: When a spouse wants to file for divorce in California...
heuristics.action: The filing spouse does not need the other spouse's agreement and does not need to prove wrongdoing; divorce may be filed for any reason
heuristics.because: California operates under a no-fault model: 'You don't need your spouse's agreement to get a divorce. You can get divorced for any reason.'
heuristics.regulatory_basis: California Courts Self-Help Center (Judicial Branch of California), selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/divorce-california

heuristics.rule: In equitable distribution states (all US states not listed as community property states), courts divide marital property based on fairness factors set by state law, not a mechanical 50/50 split.
heuristics.condition: When a couple divorces in a state outside the nine community property states and Alaska opt-in...
heuristics.action: Submit to a fact-specific judicial process where factors such as marriage length, income disparity, and non-financial contributions (homemaking, supporting a spouse's career) are weighed to determine a division that may or may not be 50/50.
heuristics.because: Equitable distribution is explicitly distinct from equal distribution — the governing standard is fairness, not mathematical equality.
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Cornell Law School LII — Wex: community_property

heuristics.rule: A cohabitation agreement is the only mechanism for common-law partners in Ontario to establish enforceable property-division terms
heuristics.condition: When common-law partners in Ontario wish to create property rights or obligations between themselves
heuristics.action: Enter into a voluntary cohabitation agreement
heuristics.because: Without a cohabitation agreement, no automatic legal property-division framework applies to common-law couples in Ontario
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Government of Ontario (ontario.ca) — dividing property when marriage or common-law relationship ends

heuristics.rule: Separate treatment of 'whether to leave' vs. 'how to legally leave'
heuristics.condition: When advising someone on ending a relationship who has recently relocated to a new state...
heuristics.action: Surface the residency window requirement as a concrete, checkable fact before discussing filing mechanics — do not conflate emotional/repairability diagnosis with legal eligibility
heuristics.because: Residency requirements create a real eligibility gate that affects when and where a person can file; the two questions require different information
heuristics.regulatory_basis: California Courts Self-Help Center (Judicial Branch of California), selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/divorce-california

heuristics.rule: Never make a stay/leave decision based on a single moment of felt clarity or panic if the person has an insecure attachment style
heuristics.condition: When someone reports sudden certainty that they must leave (or must stay) following a specific interpersonal interaction...
heuristics.action: ...treat that felt certainty as a data point about their attachment state in that moment, not as a reliable signal about the relationship's actual trajectory — require pattern evidence across multiple calm moments before acting
heuristics.because: Attachment states wax and wane with momentary perceived partner warmth; insecurely attached individuals' real-time relationship assessments are generated by a moment-to-moment reactivity system, not a stable evaluative one

heuristics.rule: One or two abuse indicators is sufficient to exit the standard relationship-decision framework entirely
heuristics.condition: When any of the 12 enumerated warning signs surface during a relationship-decision conversation...
heuristics.action: ...stop the standard repairability diagnostic and redirect immediately to the National Domestic Violence Hotline (1-800-799-SAFE, text START to 88788, or live chat at thehotline.org)
heuristics.because: The source explicitly states that even one or two behaviors constitute a red flag that abuse may be present; continuing to run a 'repairable vs. not' analysis normalizes active abuse as a garden-variety relationship problem

heuristics.rule: Assess repair attempt success rate, not conflict frequency
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether a relationship is repairable...
heuristics.action: ...ask whether repair attempts after fights usually succeed or consistently fail in the same way, rather than counting how often fights occur
heuristics.because: Gottman's research shows it is the consistent failure of repair attempts — not the presence of conflict itself — that predicts an unhappy future

heuristics.rule: Assess trust rebuilding by observable behaviors, not reported feelings
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether a partner is genuinely rebuilding trust after infidelity...
heuristics.action: ...check for three concrete behaviors: cessation of affair partner contact, voluntary transparency about whereabouts, and proactive disclosure of any accidental contact — before weighing emotional claims
heuristics.because: Feelings of readiness to trust are unfalsifiable in the moment; these behaviors are independently checkable and function as leading indicators of actual trustworthiness

heuristics.rule: When an avoidantly attached partner responds to warmth with withdrawal, diagnose the mechanism before concluding they are emotionally unavailable by preference
heuristics.condition: When one partner is being warm and the other responds with less warmth or distancing...
heuristics.action: ...distinguish whether this is a deactivating strategy (a protective response triggered by closeness cues) versus a stable preference for emotional distance, because they require entirely different interventions
heuristics.because: Avoidant attachment produces a characteristic pattern of responding to perceived partner warmth with diminished warmth — this is a protective distancing response, not a preference-based one, and misreading it as preference leads to wrong conclusions about repairability

heuristics.rule: Abuse warning signs are a categorical override, not additional data points to weigh
heuristics.condition: When a practitioner is midway through a repairability or trust-repair conversation and an abuse indicator emerges...
heuristics.action: ...treat the indicator as a hard stop rather than a factor to balance against positive relationship qualities
heuristics.because: Framing abuse behaviors as variables in a cost-benefit analysis implicitly suggests they are negotiable; the source architecture treats them as a boundary that precedes the decision framework, not inputs into it

heuristics.rule: Treat contempt as a higher-order warning signal than other negative patterns
heuristics.condition: When one or more of the Four Horsemen are present...
heuristics.action: ...weight contempt disproportionately in the repairability diagnosis relative to criticism, defensiveness, or stonewalling
heuristics.because: Gottman's research identifies contempt as 'the greatest predictor of divorce' — more than any other single factor

heuristics.rule: Treat a setback during trust rebuilding as expected process, not evidence of failure
heuristics.condition: When a regression or painful episode occurs during the trust-rebuilding period after infidelity...
heuristics.action: ...evaluate whether the behavioral commitments (no contact, transparency, proactive disclosure) remain intact rather than treating the emotional setback as proof the process has broken down
heuristics.because: Research explicitly identifies the process as non-linear; mistaking a predictable setback for process failure causes premature exit from a potentially repairable situation

heuristics.rule: Treat anxious attachment's behavioral unpredictability as a diagnostic signal, not as evidence of the partner's inconsistency
heuristics.condition: When a partner reports that the anxiously attached person is 'hot and cold' — sometimes warm in response to warmth, sometimes withdrawing...
heuristics.action: ...identify whether the unpredictable pattern tracks the anxiously attached person's internal state rather than the partner's actual behavior before attributing the instability to the relationship itself
heuristics.because: Anxious individuals do not reliably predict warmer behavior even when the partner is being warm — the inconsistency is generated internally, so attributing it to relationship dysfunction produces a misdiagnosis

heuristics.rule: Use the 5:1 positive-to-negative ratio as a quick relationship health gauge
heuristics.condition: When assessing the baseline emotional climate of a relationship...
heuristics.action: ...estimate whether positive interactions (gratitude, affection, small gestures) outnumber negative ones by at least five to one
heuristics.because: Gottman's longitudinal data links this ratio to relationship stability; falling below it correlates with deterioration

heuristics.rule: Distinguish punitive surveillance from trust-building accountability
heuristics.condition: When the betrayed partner is considering or requesting concrete monitoring measures (shared location, access to messages)...
heuristics.action: ...frame and implement these as time-limited trust-building mechanisms initiated by the involved partner, not as ongoing punishment
heuristics.because: The research distinguishes accountability measures as trust signals when voluntarily offered; when experienced as punitive, they undermine rather than build the emotional safety needed for repair

heuristics.rule: Require a minimum 20-minute timeout when physiological flooding occurs during conflict
heuristics.condition: When a partner becomes emotionally overwhelmed during an argument...
heuristics.action: ...institute a hard break of at least 20 minutes and avoid ruminating on grievances during it
heuristics.because: Research shows couples who took ~30-minute discussion breaks showed significantly lower heart rates and more positive subsequent interactions; ruminating during the break negates the benefit

heuristics.rule: Require proactive disclosure of accidental contact as a binary test
heuristics.condition: When the affair partner is part of the same social, professional, or geographic environment and complete avoidance is impractical...
heuristics.action: ...treat whether the involved partner volunteers accidental contact disclosures unprompted as a hard diagnostic — this is a higher-signal behavior than the absence of deliberate contact
heuristics.because: Proactive disclosure in low-stakes accidental moments is a strong behavioral indicator of sustained commitment to transparency rather than compliance under surveillance

heuristics.rule: Reframe complaints from character attacks to specific behavioral requests
heuristics.condition: When conflict communication defaults to criticism of who the partner is...
heuristics.action: ...shift to 'I' statements describing a specific behavior and an expressed need, not a verdict on character
heuristics.because: Criticism of character activates defensiveness and contempt; behavior-specific 'I' statements create space for repair rather than escalation

heuristics.rule: Use time-with-no-visible-progress as the outcome-level leave signal, not conflict intensity alone
heuristics.condition: When a couple has repeated conflict without resolution, ongoing anxiety, and emotional withdrawal that never gets resolved...
heuristics.action: ...treat the persistence and non-resolution over time as the primary indicator, not the mere presence of conflict or anxiety
heuristics.because: Conflict is present in repairable relationships too; what distinguishes them is whether the pattern moves — repeated conflict without progress over time is the distinguishing marker

heuristics.rule: If the urge to leave arose immediately after a spike in closeness or vulnerability, treat that urge as suspect until you can distinguish it from deactivation
heuristics.condition: When an avoidantly attached person feels sudden, strong clarity that the relationship is wrong or that they want to leave
heuristics.action: Ask whether the certainty followed a moment of increased intimacy, dependency, or emotional exposure — if yes, flag it as a possible deactivating strategy rather than genuine incompatibility
heuristics.because: Avoidant deactivation produces feelings that are experientially indistinguishable from authentic preference, so the felt certainty itself is not reliable evidence of the relationship's actual state

heuristics.rule: Establish safety before attempting problem-solving
heuristics.condition: When a couple is in conflict and trying to resolve a substantive issue...
heuristics.action: ...restore emotional safety and reconnect first before introducing the topic to be solved
heuristics.because: Without emotional safety, the thinking brain is inaccessible, so any proposed solution will fail regardless of its quality

heuristics.rule: One partner's unwillingness to work on the recurring pattern is a hard leave signal
heuristics.condition: When one partner consistently refuses to engage with or address the identified repeating pattern...
heuristics.action: ...treat that unwillingness as a load-bearing decision factor, not a temporary obstacle to route around
heuristics.because: Mutual willingness to change is identified as the central repair-viability test; without it, effort by the willing partner cannot close the gap

heuristics.rule: Petty or suddenly-noticed flaws in a partner's appearance, habits, or minor behaviors are a diagnostic signal of deactivation, not evidence of incompatibility
heuristics.condition: When an avoidantly attached person begins cataloguing small, previously tolerable partner behaviors as deal-breakers
heuristics.action: Treat the timing and triviality of the complaints as data about the attachment system's state, not as objective evidence that the partner has changed or that the relationship is broken
heuristics.because: Avoidants manufacture reasons to exit as a proximity-regulation mechanism; the reasons feel real but are generated by the anxiety of closeness, not by genuine incompatibility

heuristics.rule: Distinguish the source of pain before deciding whether to repair or leave
heuristics.condition: When a partner is feeling relationship pain and is unsure whether to stay or go...
heuristics.action: ...ask whether the pain comes from what is missing (depletion) or from what has been done (breakage), and use that answer as the first fork in the decision
heuristics.because: Depleted relationships lack fuel but retain structural integrity; broken relationships have fractured foundations that require a different — often irrecoverable — kind of work

heuristics.rule: Reframe ending the relationship as a needs-assessment verdict, not a past-value verdict
heuristics.condition: When someone is stuck on 'but we had good years' as a reason to stay despite ongoing unmet needs...
heuristics.action: ...explicitly separate the question 'did this relationship matter' from the question 'is this relationship meeting my needs now and going forward'
heuristics.because: The distortion that ending equals invalidating the past is a known cognitive block; decoupling past validity from current functionality unblocks the decision

heuristics.rule: Map whether the desire to leave built gradually and independently of intimacy events, or spiked after closeness increased — the trajectory distinguishes real incompatibility from deactivation-as-false-clarity
heuristics.condition: When assessing whether an avoidant person's relationship dissatisfaction is a signal worth acting on
heuristics.action: Reconstruct the timeline: if dissatisfaction tracks intimacy spikes, weight it as likely deactivation; if it built independently over time, weight it as more likely reflecting the relationship's actual state
heuristics.because: The same internal experience (wanting to leave) has different causal origins, and only the origin determines whether leaving is the right response

heuristics.rule: Treat contempt as a categorically different signal from ordinary conflict
heuristics.condition: When assessing whether a couple's negative patterns are repairable...
heuristics.action: ...check specifically for contempt rather than just frequency or intensity of conflict; if contempt has replaced conflict, treat this as a 'let go' indicator
heuristics.because: Contempt specifically predicts relationship failure in a way that other conflict behaviors do not

heuristics.rule: Layer outcome-level checks on top of mechanism-level checks, never instead of them
heuristics.condition: When using signs like 'ongoing anxiety' or 'no progress' to evaluate a relationship...
heuristics.action: ...also separately ask whether the apparent no-progress is an attachment-mechanism artifact (deactivation resetting, hyperactivation misreading distance) before concluding the relationship is the cause
heuristics.because: Outcome-level signs alone will misfire on couples where one partner's deactivation cycle resets every time closeness approaches, producing the appearance of a stuck relationship when the mechanism, not the relationship, is the primary driver

heuristics.rule: Require both partners' willingness as a minimum condition before recommending repair
heuristics.condition: When one partner is doing all the repair work and the other is not engaged...
heuristics.action: ...treat asymmetric effort as a hard stop on the repair path rather than a problem to be solved through more effort by the willing partner
heuristics.because: Repair requires two participants; sustained unilateral effort without reciprocation is a structural condition, not a temporary gap

heuristics.rule: Apply abuse as a hard override that pre-empts the depleted/broken diagnostic framework entirely
heuristics.condition: When any form of active abuse is present — physical, emotional, financial, or sexual...
heuristics.action: ...exit the diagnostic framework and treat leaving as the indicated path before running any other analysis
heuristics.because: Abuse is not a repair problem; running a repairability diagnosis in an abuse context delays safety and implicitly treats a safety issue as a relationship-quality issue

heuristics.rule: Treat a partner's shift from emotional distress to quiet detachment as a terminal warning signal, not a sign things have calmed down
heuristics.condition: When a previously expressive, communicative partner becomes polite, distant, and emotionally flat
heuristics.action: Recognize this as the final stage of emotional withdrawal — the relationship is likely already over in their mind even if they haven't left yet
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters and the OP describe this pattern: the partner stopped crying, stopped asking, stopped fighting — and that silence marked the end, not a resolution. 'By the time I wanted to fix things, she was already healing from the damage I caused.'

heuristics.rule: If you've been dumped, withdrawal and silence is more effective than pursuing or arguing
heuristics.condition: When you are the one who was broken up with and want to preserve any chance of reconnection
heuristics.action: Go no contact, focus on yourself, and let your absence do the communicating
heuristics.because: Multiple comments converge on the idea that pursuing someone who ended the relationship signals low self-worth and pushes them further away; the dumped person has no leverage to 'fight' directly

heuristics.rule: Cut contact entirely in the immediate aftermath of a breakup — delete socials, block if necessary — before attempting any closure conversation
heuristics.condition: When you have just broken up and feel the urge to reach out, seek closure, or monitor their activity
heuristics.action: Remove all live connections to the person (social media, messaging apps, saved contact) before attempting any further communication
heuristics.because: Each interaction re-activates the nervous system's attachment response, resetting the neurological unlearning process and prolonging the acute pain phase

heuristics.rule: Judge long-term relationship viability by consistent actions over time, not by the intensity or frequency of verbal declarations
heuristics.condition: When a partner has made strong verbal commitments (soulmate language, promise rings, 'forever' talk) early or throughout the relationship...
heuristics.action: Weight their sustained behavioral patterns — reliability, reciprocity, showing up during difficulty — far more heavily than the words themselves
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters independently noted that partners who used the strongest romantic language ('soulmate', 'my person', 'love of my life') were the same ones who ended the relationship abruptly, suggesting grand verbal proclamations are weakly predictive of actual commitment

heuristics.rule: Redirect the love you gave your partner toward yourself as the first step in recovery
heuristics.condition: When you have lost a partner who was your primary emotional anchor and you are struggling to find motivation to heal
heuristics.action: Consciously reinvest the same attention, care, and energy you gave the relationship into your own wellbeing, hobbies, and self-development
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters independently described having poured themselves entirely into a partner at the expense of self-care, and identified that redirecting that energy inward was the turning point in recovery

heuristics.rule: If you were already giving 100% and they still left, repeating the same behavior post-breakup will not change the outcome
heuristics.condition: When you were the one carrying the relationship and the partner still ended it...
heuristics.action: Stop begging, chasing, or trying to prove yourself — those behaviors replay the same failed dynamic
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters converge on the idea that the effort mismatch was the core problem; more effort from the same person does not fix a structural incompatibility

heuristics.rule: Do not enter a relationship unless you have genuine capacity — emotional, practical, life-stage — to sustain it
heuristics.condition: When considering starting or continuing a relationship where one partner is not in a position to fully show up
heuristics.action: Decline to pursue or continue rather than occupy space in someone's life you cannot fill
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters converged on the idea that entering without capacity causes downstream harm to the other person's future — stated explicitly as 'take your hands off another person's future'

heuristics.rule: Stop all contact attempts after a breakup before attempting any reconnection
heuristics.condition: When you have just broken up and are tempted to text, call, or show up to reverse the outcome immediately
heuristics.action: Implement a hard no-contact period and use it to do actual self-work rather than as a strategic timer
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters corroborate that continued contact (texting, showing up at work, begging friends) only pushed the ex further away, while the break in contact created the space for the ex to re-initiate

heuristics.rule: Do not pursue new romantic relationships for at least one year after a significant breakup
heuristics.condition: When you have just ended a serious relationship and feel the urge to start dating again to fill the void
heuristics.action: Wait at least one year before pursuing someone new; focus on friends, family, and solo healing instead
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters noted that unresolved feelings leak into new relationships, and that the skill of thriving alone is the most valuable outcome of the healing period — rushing rebounds hurts the other person and delays your own recovery

heuristics.rule: No contact means no contact permanently, not temporarily
heuristics.condition: When you have decided to end contact with an ex after a breakup
heuristics.action: Treat no contact as a permanent default, not a strategy to win them back or a pause
heuristics.because: Multiple comments reinforce that any re-engagement (even responding to breadcrumb messages like 'Merry Christmas') resets the emotional detox process and re-exposes you to the same patterns

heuristics.rule: When a partner's stated reason for breaking up does not match their subsequent behavior, treat the stated reason as a cover story
heuristics.condition: When an ex cites moral, religious, or emotional reasons for ending a relationship but immediately returns to dating apps or casual behavior
heuristics.action: Discount the stated reason entirely and focus on the behavioral evidence of their actual intent
heuristics.because: The OP's ex cited religious guilt but was found on Bumble with a casual-sex profile within the same period — multiple commenters reinforced that actions reveal intent more reliably than tearful explanations

heuristics.rule: No contact after a breakup is the default protective move, not a strategy to get someone back
heuristics.condition: When a relationship has ended and one party is still emotionally attached...
heuristics.action: Implement no contact and treat it as permanent rather than as a waiting period
heuristics.because: Multiple comments indicate that continuing contact while hoping for reconciliation prolongs pain without changing the outcome — the ex has already made their decision

heuristics.rule: Remove the ex from your social media and stop viewing theirs to accelerate emotional recovery
heuristics.condition: When you are stuck in grief after a breakup and struggling to move on...
heuristics.action: Remove them from your social feeds and do not look at their profiles
heuristics.because: A commenter with personal experience of years-long attachment noted that continued social media exposure sustains the hope of reconciliation, which is the primary mechanism keeping people emotionally stuck

heuristics.rule: When a family member's hostility toward you is extreme and inexplicable by surface-level reasons, suspect an undisclosed relational secret before attributing it to personality or malice alone
heuristics.condition: When a sibling or close family member displays disproportionate, lifelong hatred toward a specific person with no clear rational cause
heuristics.action: Treat the hostility as a potential signal of concealed parentage, trauma history, or forced family arrangement — seek clarifying information before internalizing blame
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters in this thread independently noted that extreme hostility from a 'sibling' was later explained by concealed parentage and reproductive trauma, suggesting the pattern recurs across families

heuristics.rule: When a friend suddenly ghosts after a shared crisis, check whether a controlling partner is mediating their behavior before assuming the friend is angry at you
heuristics.condition: When a close friend goes silent after an emotionally intense shared event and their partner has already sent a hostile message on their behalf
heuristics.action: Route concern and outreach through a mutual friend rather than continuing to message directly, and prioritize checking on the friend's safety over resolving your own guilt
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters with lived experience of abusive relationships identified the blocking/ghosting pattern as a protective measure the controlled partner takes to shield both themselves and the OP from further escalation — not as rejection

heuristics.rule: When a partner responds to being caught cheating with anger, door-slamming, and silent treatment rather than remorse or explanation, treat the anger as confirmation — not ambiguity.
heuristics.condition: When a partner who has been suspected of cheating reacts to discovery with fury directed at the person who found out, rather than with defensiveness about the accusation itself...
heuristics.action: Stop seeking confirmation through conversation; the behavioral response is itself the answer. Begin exit planning.
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters converged on the point that his rage at being caught — not at the accusation — is the tell. One commenter stated: 'He knows it's wrong and he's mad he got caught.'

heuristics.rule: Tell your partner immediately when you discover third-party interference in your relationship, even if discovery was accidental
heuristics.condition: When you accidentally discover that a family member has been sending cruel or manipulative messages to your partner behind your back...
heuristics.action: Acknowledge how you found out, affirm you are on their side, and act on the information rather than sitting on it
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters converged on this: the partner has been carrying the burden alone, and continued silence compounds the harm and erodes safety in the relationship

heuristics.rule: When a partner has committed reproductive coercion, treat the relationship as non-repairable immediately — do not negotiate, do not explain, do not seek closure through conversation with the perpetrator.
heuristics.condition: When a partner has deliberately sabotaged birth control or otherwise violated bodily autonomy to force a pregnancy...
heuristics.action: Exit the relationship with minimal contact; do not brief the perpetrator on your reproductive decisions; use legal channels if communication is required.
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters converged on the position that the act constitutes sexual assault and that continued engagement exposes the victim to further coercion or retaliation. The informed commenter explicitly stated 'This man is dangerous' and advised ghosting after moving out.

heuristics.rule: A partner's behavior during your medical vulnerability is one of the most reliable tests of actual care vs. performed care
heuristics.condition: When a partner does household tasks and appears functional day-to-day but has never had to sacrifice convenience for your wellbeing...
heuristics.action: ...treat a genuine medical emergency or vulnerability moment as a diagnostic event — their response reveals baseline empathy level more accurately than routine behavior
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters noted that the husband's indifference to OP passed out on the floor — then blaming her — was more revealing than years of doing chores, because chores carry no personal cost

heuristics.rule: When a partner uses third-party institutions (police, legal systems) as weapons against you and then minimizes it as a 'mistake,' treat it as a pattern signal, not an isolated incident
heuristics.condition: When a partner involves authorities in a way that harms, humiliates, or destabilizes you — and then acts loving immediately after —
heuristics.action: Do not accept the 'mistake' framing; assess whether this fits a control or punishment dynamic rather than a misunderstanding
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters with direct experience described this exact sequence — involve cops, act cuddly, gaslight — as a documented abuse tactic used to destabilize and control

heuristics.rule: Document the state of the shared space before leaving — timestamped photos or video sent immediately to a third party
heuristics.condition: When vacating a shared apartment after a relationship breakdown, especially on short notice
heuristics.action: Take timestamped photos/video of every room showing the apartment undamaged, then immediately send them to the leasing office or a trusted third party
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters independently flagged this: without documentation, an ex can damage the property and claim you caused it, exposing you to deposit loss or legal liability

heuristics.rule: When a trusted person in a professional role breaches your confidence once, treat it as a pattern, not a one-time mistake — remove them from your professional life regardless of personal relationship
heuristics.condition: When someone you trusted with sensitive financial or legal information disclosed it to a third party, even if they apologized
heuristics.action: Move your business to a new professional immediately and do not give them access to sensitive information again
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters independently noted that a single breach is evidence of a pattern ('if you catch them it's probably happened before') and the structural incentive to re-offend remains unchanged

heuristics.rule: Judge a partner's character by how they treat people they are NOT attracted to or invested in, not by how they treat you
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether a partner's kindness toward you reflects genuine character...
heuristics.action: Observe how they speak about and treat people outside their social or attractiveness hierarchy — strangers, waitstaff, people they find unattractive
heuristics.because: Multiple comments converge on the point that the boyfriend's cruelty was only visible when he didn't know the target was OP — his 'niceness' to her was conditional on her fitting his attractiveness standard, not a reflection of character

heuristics.rule: When retrieving belongings from a potentially unsafe ex's home, bring multiple people and avoid notifying the ex of the exact timing
heuristics.condition: When a partner has shown controlling or coercive behavior during a breakup and you need to collect your things
heuristics.action: Coordinate retrieval for a time you are certain they are away (e.g., confirmed work hours), bring multiple trusted people, and consider a police escort
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters flagged the ex's coercive behavior as a safety concern and one commenter described personally using a police escort for the same situation, suggesting this is a recognized protective measure in the community

heuristics.rule: When physical violence occurs once (throwing objects, strangulation), treat it as a terminal event — not a data point to weigh against prior good behavior
heuristics.condition: When a partner escalates to throwing objects or physical strangulation, regardless of prior relationship history
heuristics.action: Leave immediately, involve law enforcement, pursue all legal protections (restraining orders, court hearings)
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters — including a self-identified therapist and psychologist — independently stated that this level of violence indicates willingness to kill; waiting for a second incident dramatically increases lethality risk

heuristics.rule: Document the state of shared living spaces before departing — video and email to landlord
heuristics.condition: When leaving a shared apartment after a breakup...
heuristics.action: Take a video of the entire apartment after packing, leave keys in the mailbox, and email the leasing office with the video as a timestamped record
heuristics.because: OP explicitly did this and multiple commenters validated it as protective; it creates a paper trail against future disputes over damage deposits or property claims

heuristics.rule: Document neglect and extreme behavior before filing for divorce when children are involved
heuristics.condition: When a partner exhibits radicalization, neglect of children, or erratic behavior and custody is at stake...
heuristics.action: Begin systematic documentation of incidents, financial irregularities, and neglect before initiating legal proceedings
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters and OP's lawyer confirmed that documented evidence of neglect and misconduct directly strengthened the custody case; the paper trail converted a 'might have a chance' into a strong case

heuristics.rule: Set explicit mutual gift budgets before holidays, not after the disappointment
heuristics.condition: When entering a serious relationship where gift-giving expectations are unclear
heuristics.action: Verbally agree on a budget and expectation level for birthdays and holidays before the occasion arrives
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters noted that unspoken expectations create asymmetric effort and resentment; one commenter explicitly recommended setting a budget 'verbally and together so he knows what he should aim for'

heuristics.rule: Three-year minimum for grief recovery after catastrophic parental loss
heuristics.condition: When a partner loses both parents suddenly and simultaneously, and the grieving person is showing withdrawal, weight gain, and emotional shutdown...
heuristics.action: Do not set a one-year recovery expectation; use three years as the minimum realistic window before projecting normalcy
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters who personally experienced major parental loss independently cited timelines of 4-10 years before functional recovery; one commenter noted a minimum of four years before being able to discuss the loss without crying

heuristics.rule: The behavior surrounding a secret matters more than the secret itself
heuristics.condition: When a partner refuses to disclose something and responds with defensiveness, gaslighting, and refusal to cooperate...
heuristics.action: Treat the behavioral pattern as the primary diagnostic signal, regardless of what the hidden thing turns out to be
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters noted that even if the content of the locked room was innocent, the husband's refusal, gaslighting, and dismissal of her concerns were themselves serious relationship violations independent of what was hidden

heuristics.rule: When you hide a gift early, immediately document its location with a photo or note
heuristics.condition: When you purchase a gift well in advance and hide it to prevent accidental discovery...
heuristics.action: Take a photo of the hiding spot immediately and store it in a password-protected note on your phone
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters with ADHD and general forgetfulness independently converged on this solution — photos work better than written notes for impulsive-memory types because they require less friction in the moment

heuristics.rule: When friends independently and consistently avoid your partner, treat it as diagnostic data about your relationship, not a social management problem
heuristics.condition: When multiple friends from different contexts all express discomfort around your partner and decline to socialize with them
heuristics.action: Treat the consensus as external signal about in-relationship dynamics you may have normalized, and bring it explicitly into therapy
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters noted that unanimous friend avoidance suggests behavior more severe than the partner may be perceiving — the outsider view cuts through normalization

heuristics.rule: When a partner frames opening the relationship while simultaneously blocking the other partner from doing the same, the stated reason (polyamory identity) is not the real driver — the real driver is a specific external interest.
heuristics.condition: When a spouse comes out as polyamorous but becomes visibly distressed or obstructive when the other partner attempts to also date
heuristics.action: Treat the asymmetric enforcement as diagnostic evidence of bad faith, not a feature of their polyamory identity
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters with lived poly experience noted this pattern — the husband both demanded freedom and became 'on the verge of a breakdown' when OP tried to meet someone for coffee, which experienced poly community members identify as a recurring red flag

heuristics.rule: Gradually reclaim household responsibilities rather than attempting a sudden full reversal
heuristics.condition: When one partner has absorbed nearly all domestic labor and the other has lost the habit of contributing
heuristics.action: Start with one task, own it consistently, then add another the following month until the split is roughly equitable
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters independently converged on the incremental approach ('start small', 'pick his least favorite chore', 'gradually increase') as the mechanism for rebuilding capability without triggering conflict

heuristics.rule: When a partner is consistently absent during a medical crisis, treat it as a relationship-ending data point, not a rough patch
heuristics.condition: When a partner repeatedly fails to show up across multiple, escalating medical events (appointments, surgery, post-op care) despite explicit requests
heuristics.action: Begin exit planning rather than further attempts at repair, starting with securing personal assets and consulting a lawyer
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters independently converged on the same conclusion — this pattern of behavior across distinct events signals not a temporary lapse but a stable disposition of indifference or hostility

heuristics.rule: You cannot solve a mental health problem that belongs to your partner and that they refuse to treat
heuristics.condition: When a partner's untreated mental health condition is the primary driver of recurring conflict
heuristics.action: Stop attempting to manage or accommodate the condition yourself; require the partner to seek professional treatment as a condition of continuing the relationship
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters independently stated that the disorder is the husband's responsibility to manage, not the wife's to absorb — and that untreated conditions do not improve through the partner's accommodation alone

heuristics.rule: Therapy is not optional after betrayal — it is the mechanism for understanding why you chose the relationship in the first place, which prevents repeating the pattern
heuristics.condition: When recovering from infidelity or a relationship ending due to a partner's fundamental character failure...
heuristics.action: Prioritize therapy explicitly focused on 'the why' — why you settled, what needs the relationship met, what warning signs you rationalized — not just processing the immediate grief
heuristics.because: OP explicitly states she would not have built her current life without therapy working out 'the why of me settling for this man in the first place,' and names it as the prerequisite to all other positive outcomes

heuristics.rule: Use a direct, honest confrontation conversation as a diagnostic test — not a repair attempt
heuristics.condition: When you are unsure whether a partner is capable of change and want a definitive signal before deciding to leave
heuristics.action: Raise the core issue calmly and observe whether they listen and take responsibility, or immediately deflect and attack you
heuristics.because: The OP explicitly framed the conversation this way: 'If he showed sincerity, maybe we'd try one more time. If not… well, you know.' The partner's defensive blow-up gave her the answer without requiring further deliberation.

heuristics.rule: When leaving a potentially controlling or abusive partner, bring a group escort for the physical move — do not go alone
heuristics.condition: When you have reason to believe the partner may become volatile, manipulative, or attempt to block your exit during a move-out
heuristics.action: Arrange multiple people to accompany you to the property; the presence of witnesses deters escalation and provides physical safety
heuristics.because: OP's account confirms the partner stayed home unexpectedly; having a group present caused him to leave and give limited time to pack — the escort directly enabled a safe exit

heuristics.rule: When a partner backtracks on a breakup threat rather than following through, treat the threat itself — not the backtracking — as the signal about who they are
heuristics.condition: When a partner issues a controlling ultimatum, then retreats to 'it was a joke' when called on it
heuristics.action: Use the original threat as the data point for decision-making, not the subsequent retreat
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters noted that the backtracking was predictable and did not change the meaning of the original behavior — the threat revealed the control dynamic regardless of whether it was executed

heuristics.rule: Address the 'why' behind the behavior, not just the behavior itself
heuristics.condition: When a partner's negative reaction to your interests feels disproportionate or comes with emotional charge...
heuristics.action: Dig into the root experience or fear driving the reaction before asking for behavioral change
heuristics.because: The girlfriend's disgust reactions stemmed from past negative associations with people who shared those hobbies, not from her actual feelings about the OP — addressing only the surface behavior would have left the underlying fear unresolved

heuristics.rule: Use your own psychological and emotional state as a diagnostic instrument for relationship health
heuristics.condition: When you notice you have become chronically anxious, irritable, pessimistic, or unrecognizable to your former self inside a relationship...
heuristics.action: Treat that personal deterioration as a concrete signal that the relationship is damaging you, and seriously evaluate leaving
heuristics.because: The highest-upvoted answer directly frames personal psychological regression — hysteria, anxiety, loss of gentleness, pessimism, low confidence — as the primary indicator that a relationship should end, grounding the rule in observed self-change rather than partner behavior alone

heuristics.rule: Before attempting reconciliation, verify that the structural obstacle causing the breakup can actually be resolved
heuristics.condition: When a breakup was caused by a concrete external barrier (long-distance, parental opposition, financial dependency)
heuristics.action: Ask yourself whether you are genuinely willing to take the action needed to remove that barrier; if not, do not pursue reconciliation
heuristics.because: Multiple comments agree that reconciling without resolving the root cause creates a repeating cycle — the same problem resurfaces after reunion

heuristics.rule: Match reconnection intensity to breakup severity — don't force no-contact when a light-touch approach works better
heuristics.condition: When the breakup is mild (contact still exists, ex responds to non-romantic topics without hostility)...
heuristics.action: Maintain weak contact (every few days, 3-5 messages, no mention of feelings) rather than enforcing a full no-contact period
heuristics.because: Forced no-contact in a light breakup creates artificial distance where none is needed, and can be read as indifference, pushing the ex further away

heuristics.rule: Use the presence of the breakup question itself as a signal
heuristics.condition: When someone is asking whether they should break up...
heuristics.action: Treat the act of asking as evidence that a serious doubt already exists — then investigate whether the doubt is about the person or just a rough patch
heuristics.because: Top-ranked comment explicitly states: asking the question already signals a breakup impulse has formed; the more useful question is whether mutual attraction still exists

heuristics.rule: Match trust-rebuilding strategy to partner's attachment style, not to a generic apology script
heuristics.condition: When attempting to rebuild trust after a breach...
heuristics.action: First identify whether the partner is secure, anxious, avoidant, or disorganized/fearful, then apply style-specific strategies: for secure types, acknowledge the breach and demonstrate concrete change; for avoidant types, identify unspoken micro-expectations and meet them quietly without pressure; for anxious types, increase energy investment and provide accurate emotional responses before making promises
heuristics.because: The top answer (6083 chars, highest rank) argues that trust is defined by perceived consistency, predictability, and reliability — and each attachment style has a different internal model of what those mean, so a single approach fails across types

heuristics.rule: Categorize the reason for wanting to leave before deciding whether to leave
heuristics.condition: When you are considering a breakup but are unsure whether the problem is real or solvable
heuristics.action: Identify whether the dissatisfaction is (a) a persistent character trait you cannot accept, (b) a faded feeling that may be normalcy vs. genuine loss of love, or (c) an external obstacle that could be overcome with effort — then apply different logic to each category
heuristics.because: The top-ranked answer explicitly distinguishes these three categories and argues that the correct response differs entirely depending on which type of problem is driving the impulse to leave

heuristics.rule: Pre-emptively stating your dealbreakers does not protect you — it only clarifies the cost after the breach.
heuristics.condition: When you explicitly tell a partner early on that deception is a hard boundary...
heuristics.action: Do not treat the verbal agreement as a guarantee; treat their subsequent behavior as the only real signal.
heuristics.because: The poster explicitly warned her boyfriend before the relationship began, yet the deception started within the first year. The pre-emptive statement changed nothing operationally — it only made the betrayal legible in retrospect.

heuristics.rule: Repeated forgiveness without changed behavior trains the offending partner to expect continued tolerance
heuristics.condition: When one partner consistently forgives without the other making concrete behavioral change
heuristics.action: Recognize that unconditional forgiveness, absent accountability, creates a cycle where the offending partner subconsciously learns there are no real consequences
heuristics.because: OP states explicitly: 'Every time she forgave me... I subconsciously learned that I could mess up again and still be okay.' This is corroborated by multiple commenters who described identical dynamics with their own partners.

heuristics.rule: Both parties must be willing to do the work for a reconnection to be viable
heuristics.condition: When considering whether to attempt reconciliation after a breakup
heuristics.action: Assess whether the other person is actively open-minded and communicative, not just passively accepting contact
heuristics.because: The one detailed success case in the thread explicitly attributes the outcome to both parties being willing to be open-minded and communicative — commenter states 'things only worked out because both parties were willing'

heuristics.rule: If you must reach out, impose a mandatory waiting window before acting on the impulse
heuristics.condition: When the urge to contact an ex feels urgent and uncontrollable
heuristics.action: Set a minimum delay — 'in an hour', 'tomorrow', 'next week' — and try to extend it each time; even a few minutes counts as a win
heuristics.because: Urgency is a withdrawal symptom, not a signal of genuine need; the delay interrupts the automatic behavior loop

heuristics.rule: When grieving a non-toxic incompatibility breakup, distinguish between missing the specific person and missing the state of having a partner
heuristics.condition: When you find yourself in post-breakup grief after a relationship that ended without clear wrongdoing...
heuristics.action: Actively identify whether you miss this particular person or the comfort and companionship of couplehood in general before making any contact decision
heuristics.because: A commenter with community agreement explicitly articulated: 'I don't even want them back, I just miss what it felt like to have someone' — conflating the two drives premature re-contact or prolonged grief with no actionable resolution

heuristics.rule: Do not treat a partner as your entire social world — maintain an independent support network
heuristics.condition: When you are in a serious relationship and your partner has become your only close friend and confidant
heuristics.action: Actively maintain or build friendships and social ties outside the relationship
heuristics.because: Multiple posters described having made their partner their 'everything' and having no support system after the breakup, which compounded the pain and slowed recovery significantly

heuristics.rule: Full no-contact is the only reliable path through acute grief after a breakup
heuristics.condition: When you are in the first months after a relationship ends and are tempted to check on the ex...
heuristics.action: Implement full no contact — no Instagram scrolling, no texting, no asking mutual friends
heuristics.because: The original poster explicitly states it took months to cut contact and frames it as the only thing that worked; corroborated by the community tone across multiple comments

heuristics.rule: When core life-direction values diverge (children, marriage, geography, life goals), ending the relationship before resentment builds is the cleaner path
heuristics.condition: When two people have a fundamentally healthy relationship but want incompatible futures
heuristics.action: Acknowledge the incompatibility directly and separate rather than delay
heuristics.because: A commenter described ending a relationship specifically because of kids/marriage incompatibility, noting that staying would 'likely have turned into resentment' — this framing recurred in multiple comments about growing apart

heuristics.rule: Genuine detachment from the outcome is more effective than performed detachment
heuristics.condition: When attempting reconciliation or re-entering contact with an ex
heuristics.action: Do the internal work until you are genuinely indifferent to whether reconciliation happens, not just acting indifferent
heuristics.because: The OP explicitly states 'I wasn't desperately hoping for it anymore. I genuinely would have been fine either way' — multiple commenters validated this as the key shift, distinguishing it from manipulation tactics

heuristics.rule: Use a physical journal to process post-breakup emotions rather than digital notes or social media
heuristics.condition: When you are cycling through idealized memories of an ex and cannot get clarity on why the relationship actually failed
heuristics.action: Write in a physical journal daily, recording both positives and negatives of the relationship and how your feelings shift day to day
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters described how writing forces the brain to fill in gaps with truth rather than amplifying only good memories — the same cognitive distortion that makes withdrawal from a person feel like addiction withdrawal

heuristics.rule: When an ex sends low-investment breadcrumb messages, do not respond with emotional engagement
heuristics.condition: When an ex reaches out with minimal, ambiguous messages after the breakup
heuristics.action: Ignore entirely or respond with polite indifference — do not provide an emotional reaction
heuristics.because: The community identifies this as the ex seeking validation, not reconciliation; giving an emotional response rewards the behavior and delays healing

heuristics.rule: Do not seek a post-breakup explanation from someone who lied to you during the breakup itself
heuristics.condition: When a partner has already demonstrated willingness to fabricate reasons for a breakup
heuristics.action: Resist the urge to confront or ask for clarification; accept that the answer you receive will not be honest and will not provide closure
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters advised OP that asking the ex about the real reason was 'pointless' — the consensus was that closure must come from within, not from someone who already lied

heuristics.rule: Willingness to do the work asymmetry is a relationship-ending signal
heuristics.condition: When one partner repeatedly initiates repair conversations and the other consistently withdraws or stays silent...
heuristics.action: Treat the asymmetry itself as the diagnosis — the relationship is functionally over regardless of what is said
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters independently describe the same pattern: one person initiating, the other clamming up, with the initiating partner eventually having to formally end it themselves

heuristics.rule: Convince yourself the relationship is permanently over — not just paused — before expecting emotional progress
heuristics.condition: When healing feels stalled and you keep cycling back to pain...
heuristics.action: Actively work to accept finality rather than leaving reconciliation open as a background possibility
heuristics.because: Commenter identified that lingering hope of 'making it work eventually' is what sustains the stuck emotional state, and that accepting permanent closure accelerates moving on

heuristics.rule: Disclosing a secret parentage identity should happen in childhood with age-appropriate framing rather than be deferred indefinitely
heuristics.condition: When grandparents are raising a child as their own and the biological parent is known
heuristics.action: Tell the child early using simplified, emotionally safe framing ('mama wasn't well and we wanted to help') rather than maintaining the fiction until adulthood
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters — including one who lived through deferred disclosure and one former adoption worker — stated that late disclosure caused lasting psychological harm and that early disclosure, even imperfect, would have been less damaging

heuristics.rule: Proactively offer concrete, specific financial remediation rather than open-ended 'I'll pay for it' gestures
heuristics.condition: When you have caused material damage to someone's property during an emergency
heuristics.action: Research the actual cost of forensic cleaning and seat replacement for the specific car, then send a check with documentation of the services — do not wait to be asked
heuristics.because: A commenter explicitly outlined this as the most logical course, and OP's own edits show the vague offer to pay was not landing — specificity signals genuine intent and removes the burden of chasing from the damaged party

heuristics.rule: Deflecting blame onto the person you wronged, especially as a repeated pattern, should be classified as emotional abuse — not merely a communication problem.
heuristics.condition: When a partner consistently reframes their own misconduct as the other person's fault...
heuristics.action: Name it as a pattern, not an incident. Evaluate the relationship accordingly.
heuristics.because: A commenter explicitly stated: 'deflecting and placing blame on someone that you in fact wronged as if they're somehow at fault is manipulation and 100% emotionally abusive when it's a repeated behavior.'

heuristics.rule: When confronting a narcissistic or controlling parent about their behavior toward your partner, keep your partner out of the conversation and redirect every deflection back to the parent's behavior
heuristics.condition: When a parent who shows narcissistic tendencies has harassed your partner and you need to set consequences...
heuristics.action: Frame the distance or consequences as a direct response to the parent's own conduct, not as a choice between the parent and partner
heuristics.because: A well-upvoted comment explicitly warned that a narcissistic parent will reframe any boundary as the partner's fault; removing the partner from the framing closes that manipulation loop

heuristics.rule: In all-party consent states, do not attempt to record admissions directly — use a consenting third party to elicit a text admission instead.

heuristics.rule: Pursue CPTSD-specific therapy (EMDR or similar) after leaving a long-term controlling relationship — general support is insufficient
heuristics.condition: When someone has been in a psychologically controlling or coercive relationship for an extended period
heuristics.action: Seek trauma-focused therapy such as EMDR or ketamine-assisted psychotherapy rather than general talk therapy alone
heuristics.because: Commenter with lived experience (8-year post-escape perspective) specifically named CPTSD processing and EMDR as necessary to address hypervigilance, nightmares, and daily functioning — not just emotional recovery

heuristics.rule: After sufficient no-contact, re-evaluate whether you still want the person before attempting any re-engagement
heuristics.condition: When the no-contact period ends
heuristics.action: Reassess whether the ex still meets your standards with a clear head, rather than automatically attempting to reconnect
heuristics.because: Comment [rank=2] notes that many people who complete a genuine healing process realize they no longer want the ex — saving wasted effort on unnecessary reconciliation
