decision_factors.factor: Whether the neglecting partner has self-awareness about the pattern
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Multiple commenters noted their partners would 'never admit this' or blamed the hurt partner for 'wanting too much.' Self-awareness is a prerequisite for change; its absence predicts recurrence.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Has the partner ever voluntarily acknowledged their role in the harm without being prompted, pressured, or cornered? Do they reframe the hurt partner's needs as excessive rather than as unmet?

decision_factors.factor: Which side of the breakup you are on (dumper vs. dumpee)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The dumpee has significantly less leverage to 'fight' for the relationship; the dumper retains agency and can re-initiate from a position of strength
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Clarify who initiated the breakup — this determines the entire strategic posture available to you

decision_factors.factor: Environmental overlap after breakup
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Sharing a living space, city, car, or frequent locations with the ex extends exposure to attachment triggers and slows nervous system adaptation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Inventory how many daily touchpoints (home, commute, neighborhood, social circle) are shared with or strongly associated with the ex

decision_factors.factor: Partner's emotional availability and healing status at time of breakup
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Multiple commenters described being left by partners who cited inability to give love fully due to being 'unhealed' or emotionally unavailable — this pattern affects whether the breakup reflects a permanent incompatibility or a timing/readiness issue, which changes the repairability calculus
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether the stated reason for breakup was about the relationship itself or about the partner's internal state ('I can't give you what you need' vs. 'we don't work')

decision_factors.factor: Whether the relationship ended with closure or abruptly
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Abrupt endings without explanation ('her feelings were gone') leave the abandoned partner in a prolonged rumination loop, making it harder to accept the relationship as genuinely over
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether you received a coherent reason for the ending or whether you are still generating theories to explain what happened

decision_factors.factor: Quality of memories vs. reality of the dynamic
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Having only good memories of an ex makes recovery significantly harder and distorts the assessment of whether the relationship was actually healthy
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Distinguish between emotional memory (how it felt) and behavioral reality (what each partner actually did); good feelings can coexist with a bad dynamic

decision_factors.factor: Whether the loss of love was gradual or sudden
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A partner reporting that feelings disappeared within a week — versus over months — may signal either undisclosed prior emotional withdrawal or a fundamental incompatibility that wasn't surfaced; it changes what repair would even target
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the partner to reconstruct the timeline honestly; probe for undisclosed moments of doubt that preceded the stated endpoint

decision_factors.factor: Whether the ex's stated reason for leaving is the real reason
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Multiple commenters raised doubt that 'jealousy about guy friends' was the full story, suggesting the ex may have left for another person. If the stated reason is a cover story, self-improvement on that issue will not address the actual cause.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Cross-check the stated reason against behavioral evidence: Did she leave for someone else around the same time? Did the timeline of her pulling away correspond with a new person entering the picture?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the ex's cruelty post-breakup is a smear campaign or genuine belief
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If the ex is rewriting history to make the dumpee the villain, it signals guilt-driven coping rather than honest assessment — which changes whether reconciliation or closure is possible
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the negative narrative contradicts things they said during the relationship; ask mutual contacts what story is being told

decision_factors.factor: Whether the ex is already in a rebound relationship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A rebound signals the ex is avoiding processing the breakup, not that they have moved on healthily — this affects how much weight to give their apparent 'okayness'
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe whether the new relationship started very quickly after the breakup; the community identifies this as void-filling, not genuine new attachment

decision_factors.factor: Whether pressure to change identity (religion, name, ethnicity) was present before the breakup
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A suggestion to convert 'by name only' to preserve the relationship signals that the partner was not acting in good faith and was potentially testing compliance rather than expressing genuine values
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Recall whether ultimatums or identity-change suggestions were framed as relationship-saving options; if so, assess whether the partner would have honored them or used them as continued leverage

decision_factors.factor: Whether feelings have ended vs. whether effort has ended
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The stated reason 'I fell out of love' forecloses repair differently than 'I don't want to work on this' — the first is a state, the second is a choice
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly: is this about how you feel, or about what you're willing to do? The answer changes whether repair is even on the table

decision_factors.factor: Timing and manner of truth disclosure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Whether the person learns the truth as a child (with framing) vs. as an adult (accidentally or hostilely) significantly shapes their ability to integrate the information and their trust in the family
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Was the disclosure planned and compassionate, or did it occur via accident, a third party, or a hostile confrontation? Did caregivers have a prepared explanation?

decision_factors.factor: Whether material remediation has been made concrete and actionable
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An abstract willingness to pay does not close the loop for the damaged party. Until a specific dollar amount or replacement plan is on the table, the aggrieved party remains in limbo and resentment can compound.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Has OP gotten a real estimate? Has a check been sent or a specific offer made in writing? Or has it remained at the level of 'I'll pay whatever it costs'?

decision_factors.factor: Partner's anger profile and volatility at time of discovery
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A partner who responds to being caught with physical expressions of anger (slamming doors, intimidating behavior) rather than conversation escalates the risk calculus for the person leaving.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe whether anger is directed at the situation or at the partner who discovered the behavior. Physical intimidation signals elevated safety risk.

decision_factors.factor: Whether the partner has been absorbing the harm silently
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A partner who hides the harassment to protect you from conflict is under compounding psychological load; the longer it continues unaddressed, the more trust damage accumulates
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look for signs of behavioral withdrawal, mood shifts, or reluctance to discuss the family member; the OP noticed his girlfriend was 'smiling and laughing' while 'carrying this alone'

decision_factors.factor: Third-party involvement (in-law or family member co-conspiring)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If a partner's family actively encouraged or orchestrated reproductive coercion, leaving the partner does not remove the threat — the family unit remains a vector for continued pressure or harassment.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review pattern of in-law comments pushing pregnancy, partner's unusually high disclosure of relationship details to parent, timing correlation between in-law conversations and the sabotage.

decision_factors.factor: Direction of blame when partner is the one in need
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Consistently blaming the ill or struggling partner for their own condition ('you did this to yourself') signals contempt, not just impatience — contempt is a Gottman-documented predictor of relationship failure
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track whether the frustration-expression pattern is bidirectional (both people) or unidirectional (always directed at the person who needs help)

decision_factors.factor: Competitive or status asymmetry in the same domain
decision_factors.why_it_matters: When partners share a field of ambition but have divergent outcomes, the underperforming partner may use sabotage or punishment behaviors that are harder to attribute to other causes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether the partner has expressed envy, dismissiveness, or subtle put-downs about your success in the shared domain previously

decision_factors.factor: Legal domestic partnership registration status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Registered domestic partnership in California (or similar jurisdictions) creates formal legal ties — lease co-tenancy, insurance coverage, potential property claims — that require affirmative legal steps to dissolve, separate from the emotional breakup
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check county registration records; OP had to drive a termination form to the LA County office — this is not automatic upon separation

decision_factors.factor: Co-parenting relationship damage
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Disclosure of inheritance information to a co-parent can permanently alter the power dynamic in custody and financial negotiations, even if the information is legally irrelevant to child support
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Has the ex already used the information to make demands or change behavior? Is the co-parenting relationship now adversarial where it was not before?

decision_factors.factor: Future physical change probability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Bodies change through pregnancy, aging, stress, and injury; a partner who responds to unattractive bodies with contempt rather than neutrality poses a future risk that is not visible at peak attractiveness
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask yourself: how has this person reacted to others who gained weight, aged, or changed physically? What would happen if I became pregnant or could not maintain current fitness?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the offended party has been materially made whole
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Paying for damages (car cleaning/seat repair) removes the concrete grievance and forces any remaining anger to reveal itself as personal or ideological rather than practical — clarifying whether repair is truly possible.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm repairs are completed and costs reimbursed before attempting reconciliation; note whether the aggrieved party's anger persists after material restitution.

decision_factors.factor: Whether a partner accepts 'no' on a non-negotiable personal decision
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A partner who refuses to accept a firm, clearly articulated decision about the other person's own body is signaling a willingness to override autonomy, which predicts escalating control
decision_factors.how_to_assess: State the decision clearly and observe whether they pivot to persuasion, coercion, or acceptance; refusal to accept after multiple clear statements is the red flag

decision_factors.factor: Support network availability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: OP's isolation (deceased father, absent mother, frail grandmother, only a sister) left her without people who could provide reality-testing earlier; isolation is both a vulnerability and a factor abusers exploit
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Who can you call right now who would believe you, house you, or accompany you to court? If the answer is fewer than two people, isolation is a risk multiplier

decision_factors.factor: Whether the partner's family network knew or facilitated the cheating
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If family members introduced the affair partner or enabled the deception, leaving severs not just the partner but an entire social system that will not support the betrayed party
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the affair partner was introduced through the cheater's social circle, and whether family members knew the cheater was still in the primary relationship at the time

decision_factors.factor: Whether domestic violence has occurred and left documentable evidence
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Multiple commenters noted that a documented physical assault — especially one witnessed by police — dramatically shifts the likelihood of obtaining sole or primary custody in family court
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Police reports, medical records, restraining orders, and arrest records all constitute usable documentation in custody proceedings

decision_factors.factor: Partner's awareness that gifting mattered
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The OP explicitly mentioned the gift three times over three weeks, eliminating the 'I didn't know' defense; awareness-plus-inaction is more damning than ignorance
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether the partner had clear, repeated signals about expectations before the occasion

decision_factors.factor: Whether the grieving partner has support systems outside the relationship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If the healthy partner is the sole support system, they carry the full weight of grief processing that they are structurally unable to help with, leading to burnout
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the grieving partner is in contact with siblings, close friends, or other family; note whether they have cut ties with those people

decision_factors.factor: Whether the secret-keeping infrastructure predates the confrontation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A lock installed 6 months ago that the partner 'let go' indicates a sustained pattern of boundary-setting against the spouse, not a one-time lapse
decision_factors.how_to_assess: How long has the locked space existed? Was it installed without discussion? Has access been consistently denied or made difficult?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the underlying forgetfulness is recognized as a pattern vs. isolated incident
decision_factors.why_it_matters: OP explicitly notes this 'happens all the time' — a single incident is forgivable; a recognized pattern that now affects significant relationship moments signals a systemic issue requiring a structural fix, not just an apology
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the forgetfulness has previously caused relationship friction, missed obligations, or required the partner to compensate repeatedly

decision_factors.factor: Whether the person inside the relationship can perceive controlling or dismissive behavior in real time
decision_factors.why_it_matters: OP explicitly stated she does not register incidents in real time and only recognizes them retrospectively or when others point them out — this indicates a significant normalization effect that distorts self-assessment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track whether you notice incidents as they happen or only after reflection or external input; discuss with individual therapist

decision_factors.factor: Sequence of disclosure vs. action
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Disclosing a polyamorous identity after already having a specific target lined up suggests the disclosure is post-hoc justification rather than honest identity sharing
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: was a specific person already identified before the disclosure conversation? How quickly after disclosure did the first 'date' appear?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the caretaking dynamic was consciously chosen or drifted into
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A dynamic that drifted through convenience is more reversible than one that was explicitly negotiated as identity (e.g., the boyfriend framing it as 'making up for lost childhood') — the latter may resist renegotiation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: did both partners explicitly discuss and agree to this division, or did it evolve because it was easy and no one objected?

decision_factors.factor: Quality of the support system outside the relationship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Whether leaving is practically feasible often depends on whether the person has family, friends, or other infrastructure to fall back on — commenters specifically conditioned their 'leave now' advice on this factor
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: Do I have family or close friends who can house me, drive me to appointments, or provide emotional support? If yes, the cost of leaving drops dramatically.

decision_factors.factor: Whether the diagnosed condition is clinically validated or a self-diagnosis used to explain controlling behavior
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A legitimate diagnosis with an established treatment path is repairable; a pseudo-diagnosis used to excuse chronic jealousy and control is a character pattern, not a condition
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the diagnosis was given by a licensed clinician, whether there is an established treatment protocol (e.g., ERP for OCD), and whether the partner is willing to engage that protocol

decision_factors.factor: Presence of covert manipulation patterns before the affair was discovered
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Covert manipulation (e.g., pretending not to have a day off to force the partner to 'work harder' on planning) signals a fundamentally unsafe relationship dynamic that the affair survivor may have normalized
decision_factors.how_to_assess: In retrospect or through therapy, audit early relationship and marriage stories for moments where the partner manufactured your distress for their entertainment or to assert control

decision_factors.factor: Speed and pattern of the post-breakup 'take-back' contact
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Rapid recontact with minimizing language ('I didn't mean it like that') after escalating insults indicates a manipulation pattern, not genuine remorse — it predicts future cycles if contact is maintained
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Note whether the apology addresses the behavior or merely walks back the words; a genuine apology names the harm, not just the phrasing

decision_factors.factor: Age gap and relationship timeline (went directly from parents' home to partner)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Moving from a parental home directly into a long-term relationship with a significantly older partner removes the developmental experience of independent living — commenters flagged this as grooming-adjacent and a predictor of deeper psychological impact post-exit
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: did the person ever live independently? Was the relationship formed when one party was significantly younger and less experienced? Did the older partner accelerate cohabitation?

decision_factors.factor: Pattern of giving second, third, and fourth chances
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A person with a habitual tendency to extend repeated chances may stay in deteriorating relationships past the point where the pattern is clearly established
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Self-assess: does your default response to poor treatment involve seeking to understand rather than acting on what was demonstrated?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the hurtful behavior has an identifiable external origin vs. reflects core values
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Behavior rooted in a past bad experience or learned association is more repairable than behavior that reflects deeply held contempt or incompatibility in values
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly where the reaction comes from; listen for whether the explanation references specific experiences (as opposed to vague dismissiveness) and whether they can separate you from the trigger group

decision_factors.factor: Clarity on why the relationship exists and what you are getting from it
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Loss of a legible answer to 'why am I in this relationship and what am I gaining' signals motivational collapse, which precedes disengagement
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask yourself directly: what is the purpose of this relationship for me right now, and can I answer that question clearly and honestly?

decision_factors.factor: Whether both parties have demonstrably changed
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Reconciliation with unchanged people and unchanged circumstances reproduces the original conflict
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the specific behavior or pattern that caused the breakup; look for concrete evidence of change in both parties, not promises or intentions

decision_factors.factor: Whether the root problem is solvable
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Reconciliation without solving the core issue (e.g., emotional dysregulation, insecurity patterns, external family opposition) predicts re-breakup
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: has anything structurally changed — therapy started, circumstance altered, insight genuinely gained — or is this the same dynamic with new optimism?

decision_factors.factor: Net emotional valence of the relationship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A relationship that produces more sadness, disappointment, and suspicion than happiness is functionally damaging regardless of historical investment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track subjective emotional state over recent weeks: is the dominant feeling happiness/security or sadness/anxiety/suspicion?

decision_factors.factor: Type of trust breach: one-off high-impact event vs. accumulated negative pattern
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A single significant breach in an otherwise stable relationship is more repairable than a long accumulation of smaller breaches — the recovery path and timeline differ substantially
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: was there a discrete event (e.g., infidelity, a major lie) or a gradual erosion (e.g., chronic neglect, repeated broken promises)? The top answer distinguishes these as requiring different levels of effort and behavioral change

decision_factors.factor: Whether loss of feeling is genuine vs. hedonic adaptation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: People in long-term relationships frequently lose the acute excitement of early love and misinterpret normalcy as absence of love, leading to premature exits they later regret.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: Would I be genuinely indifferent if this person left my life, or would I feel loss? Imagine the relationship is gone — does grief appear?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the partner deflects responsibility onto the betrayed party
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A partner who responds to being caught by suggesting the betrayed person should change themselves (e.g., 'why don't you try to look more like her') is not remorseful — they are re-framing the offense as the victim's failure. This predicts future pattern repetition.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe the first unscripted response when confronted. Deflection, counter-accusations, or comparative criticism of the betrayed partner are high-weight negative signals.

decision_factors.factor: Ego and pride as barriers to accountability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Commenters across multiple replies identified ego and pride as the core mechanism preventing partners from acknowledging fault — making repair impossible even when the relationship is otherwise viable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: When confronted, does the partner shift blame, minimize, or reframe the injured party's needs as the problem? Do they pursue 'easier' replacements rather than doing internal work?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the ex has avoidant attachment tendencies
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Avoidant partners may disengage completely without signaling closure, making reconciliation attempts futile and prolonging the dumpee's uncertainty
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look for patterns: sudden silence, no explanation, history of emotional withdrawal when stressed

decision_factors.factor: Whether the breakup was wanted or unwanted
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Being dumped creates a specific psychological profile — desire to reverse the decision, idealization of the ex, self-worth damage — that requires targeted interventions different from mutual or initiator-side breakups
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify who initiated and whether you had agency; if you were dumped, flag the self-worth and idealization risks explicitly

decision_factors.factor: Whether romantic declarations were early-stage or sustained across relationship duration
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Early intense declarations ('soulmate', 'my person') made during the infatuation phase are weak predictors of long-term commitment; the same language used after years of demonstrated partnership carries more weight
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map when the strongest declarations occurred on a relationship timeline — if concentrated at the beginning and absent during difficulty, they likely reflect fantasy-phase bonding rather than evaluated commitment

decision_factors.factor: Whether the leaver showed remorse or moved on quickly
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A partner who reconnects with an ex or moves on visibly and quickly signals that the emotional investment was asymmetric, which can deepen feelings of worthlessness and distort future trust assessments
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Note the behavioral signals after the breakup — quick rebound or reconnection with a prior ex suggests the departure was planned or emotionally pre-complete before the formal ending

decision_factors.factor: Partner's attachment style — specifically avoidant patterns
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Avoidant partners can appear secure early in a relationship and only reveal their attachment style under significant relational stress, making them difficult to identify before investment is deep
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe how the partner responds to the first major rupture or stressor — avoidant behavior tends to emerge then, not during calm periods

decision_factors.factor: Relationship duration and investment level at time of breakup
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Longer relationships (4+ years, engagement) correlate with longer and more disorienting grief even when the breakup was mutual and civil — affects post-breakup recovery planning
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Note years together, milestone markers (engagement, cohabitation), and degree of life integration

decision_factors.factor: Depth and length of shared history
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Longer, more intertwined relationships produce withdrawal symptoms similar to substance addiction — the brain amplifies good memories and suppresses bad ones, distorting the person's ability to assess whether leaving was correct
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess how long the relationship lasted, how many life milestones were shared, and whether you have independent social/emotional infrastructure outside the relationship

decision_factors.factor: Whether the person leaving has done the grief work or skipped it
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Someone who left but skipped emotional processing (via rebound, distraction, or substances) will likely re-initiate contact later from unresolved attachment, not genuine desire to reconcile
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Notice if they reach out after the initial rebound period with ambiguous or nostalgic messages — the community identifies this as a predictable pattern

decision_factors.factor: Communication pattern under conflict
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Partners who go silent or withdraw under relational stress are unlikely to change that pattern without deliberate intervention; silence during critical conversations predicts future silence
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe behavior during the last 2-3 significant disagreements — did both parties engage, or did one consistently shut down?

decision_factors.factor: Access to secular, trauma-informed therapy
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Religious-based or geographically constrained therapy options may not have the framework to address concealed parentage, reproductive trauma, or family identity rupture
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether available therapists have experience with adoption, identity, or relational trauma — and whether religious framing of the family situation would bias the therapeutic support

decision_factors.factor: Depth of the pre-existing friendship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A close friend choosing to spend the day with a heavily pregnant person signals significant investment. This is not a casual acquaintance, which means the silence is more anomalous and more likely externally driven rather than a reflection of the friendship's true state.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Would this friend have been asked to stay for the day absent any emergency? Did she willingly agree? Was there warmth during the day itself?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the other woman corroborated the timeline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In ambiguous infidelity situations, independent corroboration from another party — especially one with no motive to lie to OP — shifts the evidential weight from suspicion to near-certainty.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Did the third party confirm key details (exclusivity promise, recent contact) before the boyfriend intervened to delete the evidence?

decision_factors.factor: The harassing family member's self-awareness and willingness to accept accountability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A parent who acknowledges wrongdoing is a candidate for repair; a parent who deflects, blames the partner, or reframes the confrontation as betrayal is not
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe their initial reaction to being confronted: do they center themselves or the harm caused? Multiple commenters flagged narcissistic deflection as a strong predictor of no-change

decision_factors.factor: Health risk of continuing the pregnancy
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Chronic illness or high-risk pregnancy status shifts the decision calculus on the pregnancy itself, independent of relationship status — it adds medical urgency to what might otherwise feel like a purely relational decision.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Consult with a physician about specific risk profile; OP identified herself as chronically ill with a high-risk pregnancy prognosis as a primary driver of her termination decision.

decision_factors.factor: Postpartum history as a stress-test data point
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The postpartum period is one of the most extreme caregiving stress tests in a relationship; how a partner behaved then is a high-signal predictor of how they will behave in future crises
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: during the postpartum period, did my partner increase their load proportionally to my incapacity, maintain their baseline, or actively criticize my reduced output?

decision_factors.factor: Post-incident behavioral pattern — does the partner show remorse and accountability, or minimization and pressure to drop it
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Genuine mistakes are accompanied by remorse, apology, and acceptance of the partner's distress. Abusive incidents are followed by minimization ('you should understand'), pressure to move on, and the partner positioning themselves as reasonable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Note whether the partner acknowledges the impact on you first, or immediately moves to explain why their action was justified or understandable

decision_factors.factor: Pet ownership and custody
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Pets acquired during cohabitation can be subject to ownership disputes; taking the dog immediately on departure pre-empts a contested custody situation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whose name is on vet records, adoption paperwork, or purchase receipts before leaving

decision_factors.factor: Severity of professional violation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Attorney client confidentiality breaches by staff expose the supervising attorney to bar discipline and the firm to liability — the gravity of the violation affects both the ethical weight of reporting and the likely consequence to the firm
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Was the disclosed information covered by attorney-client privilege or equivalent professional duty? Did the breach expose the client to financial or legal risk?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the harmful act was deliberate vs. unguarded
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Unguarded cruelty (said before knowing the target) is harder to explain away as a bad day or stress — it reflects an automatic, internalized attitude
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: did they know this could hurt me when they said/did it? If no, the behavior is more diagnostic of character than a deliberate argument would be

decision_factors.factor: Reaction expression pattern when confronted (fear-anger blend vs. grief)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A partner who reacts to direct questioning about reproductive sabotage with a fear-anger fusion rather than clean denial or grief may be indicating concealment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the direct question calmly and observe the emotional register of the response — pure grief reads differently from a fear-anger conflation followed by immediate exit

decision_factors.factor: In-law alliance with abuser
decision_factors.why_it_matters: OP's mother-in-law responded to news of OP's cardiac stress symptoms by expressing concern for the husband, not OP — indicating the in-law system will not be a source of support and may actively undermine OP's safety or legal case
decision_factors.how_to_assess: When you shared the health or safety issue with the in-law, whose welfare did they prioritize in their response?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the cheating partner initiated any genuine apology versus only requested reconciliation for self-interested reasons
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A partner who emails requesting to 'talk it out' without apologizing, while still saying 'I love you,' signals that reconciliation is self-serving (e.g., losing shared housing), not genuine remorse
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Read the content of any contact: does it contain an acknowledgment of wrongdoing, or only statements of need and affection that serve the cheater's interests?

decision_factors.factor: Degree of financial deception alongside ideological radicalization
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Hidden financial behavior (secret withdrawals, donations to fringe organizations, being scammed) is independent of the ideological problem — it signals a second axis of betrayal that affects practical divorce strategy
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review all joint accounts, credit cards, and shared savings vehicles; look for withdrawals that lack receipts or explanation

decision_factors.factor: Resource asymmetry in the relationship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: OP was financially stretched but still spent $400; partner had no stated financial constraint but gave nothing — the asymmetry reveals differing levels of investment, not differing abilities
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare each partner's financial capacity against their actual gifting or effort; effort-to-capacity ratio is the meaningful signal

decision_factors.factor: Recency of 'firsts without' milestones
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Each new seasonal event — first Christmas, first birthday, first anniversary of the death — is a fresh smaller tragedy that reactivates grief; the first year is therefore the densest concentration of these triggers
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map out whether the couple is still within the first calendar year of the loss, which concentrates all first-time milestones

decision_factors.factor: Vulnerability of the discovering partner
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Pregnancy, toddler care, and financial or social dependency on the concealing partner increase the cost of leaving and may affect the urgency of safety planning
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Is the concerned partner pregnant, primary caregiver, financially dependent, or socially isolated from support networks?

decision_factors.factor: Presence of CPTSD or trauma history affecting self-judgment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: OP disclosed CPTSD, which she acknowledged makes it hard to trust her own judgment — this creates a known bias that can cause under-recognition of mistreatment and over-attribution of problems to herself
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Work with individual therapist to separate CPTSD-driven self-doubt from accurate perception; cross-reference therapist's independent assessment

decision_factors.factor: Financial and functional dependency
decision_factors.why_it_matters: When the distressed partner is also the primary earner and primary household manager, the psychological toll of the relationship conflict directly threatens financial stability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: OP reports income supporting most of the household, inability to stay on top of finances, and deteriorating physical health — the relationship harm is producing material harm

decision_factors.factor: Partner's reaction when the less-contributing person tries to re-engage
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Commenters warned 'he will probably protest and stop you' — if the caretaking partner actively resists the other person reclaiming tasks, the dynamic has crossed from generosity into control
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Attempt to take on a task unilaterally and observe the response: supportive, neutral, or blocking

decision_factors.factor: Asset ownership clarity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Jointly used property (especially cars) becomes a point of contention at separation; items with traceable provenance (gift from parent) may be treated differently than marital assets depending on jurisdiction
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify which assets were gifts from family, which were purchased jointly, and which are titled in whose name. Consult a lawyer before making any moves.

decision_factors.factor: Isolation from support network
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Concealing a partner's problematic behavior from friends and family to protect the partner's reputation removes the external reality-check that would otherwise help the person evaluate the relationship accurately
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: Have you told anyone close to you about the recurring pattern? If not, what is preventing you?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the affair partner was someone the betrayed partner was explicitly told not to worry about
decision_factors.why_it_matters: This pattern — reassurance about a specific person followed by an affair with that person — indicates deliberate deception and premeditation, not a spontaneous lapse, which sharply reduces repairability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether pre-discovery reassurances about specific individuals were given; if yes, the deception was active and sustained, not reactive

decision_factors.factor: Whether the leaving person has a safe destination secured in advance
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Having a concrete safe location to move to determines whether a clean break is logistically possible without negotiation or return
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm housing, transport, and a support network are in place before initiating the exit — OP had a destination 'a few hours away' which made no-car stalking implausible

decision_factors.factor: Quality of communication infrastructure already present in the relationship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A rough patch is more repairable when both partners can already access emotional vulnerability together; without that, the difficult conversation itself becomes an obstacle
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Have they cried together before? Can both partners move from defensive to open during a hard conversation? Multiple commenters noted the productive, emotionally honest conversation as itself a sign of relationship health

decision_factors.factor: Whether core recurring problems have been actively resolved vs. merely paused
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Unresolved problems accumulate and eventually become terminal; external improvements (ending long distance, career stability) do not substitute for internal relationship repair
decision_factors.how_to_assess: List the main recurring conflicts or issues from the past year — has each been explicitly addressed, changed, and stayed changed, or do they re-emerge?

decision_factors.factor: Genuine love vs. attachment-driven distress
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Post-breakup distress is partly neurological (Zeigarnik effect, loss aversion) and distorts perception of the ex's value; decisions made in this state are systematically biased
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Wait until emotional equilibrium returns and reassess the ex's actual qualities — multiple commenters note that people who complete genuine healing frequently conclude the ex was not as valuable as they believed

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check all platforms; classify as light/medium/heavy based on responsiveness and hostility level

decision_factors.factor: Presence of unforgivable vs. ordinary-flaw behaviors
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The top comment distinguishes between ordinary partner flaws (bad temper, gaming habits, low initiative) — which are inherent to the person and should be accepted — vs. genuinely unacceptable acts that override attraction
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Separate the complaint list into: 'personality traits I knew or should have known' vs. 'actions that cross a line I cannot accept'; only the latter category justifies exit independent of attraction

decision_factors.factor: Whether the betrayed partner is still emotionally invested in the relationship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Trust-rebuilding tactics only function if the betrayed partner has residual positive feelings; if they have emotionally exited, repair attempts may backfire or be rejected entirely
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe whether the betrayed partner engages at all — curiosity about the offending partner's changed behavior (noted in comment [rank=2]) is a positive signal; complete indifference signals emotional exit

decision_factors.factor: Whether external obstacles are truly irresolvable
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Parental disapproval, long distance, and divergent life plans feel like hard stops but often are not — couples who mistake surmountable obstacles for dealbreakers end relationships unnecessarily.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: Have both parties actually tried to solve this obstacle, or has it simply been accepted as fixed? Is the obstacle permanent or time-limited?

decision_factors.factor: Geographic and social isolation of the betrayed partner
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A partner who relocated specifically for the relationship has elevated stakes — social network disruption, logistical dependency, and sunk cost — all of which distort their capacity to evaluate the relationship clearly.

decision_factors.factor: Timing of growth relative to relationship presence
decision_factors.why_it_matters: OP describes becoming the person his partner needed only after she left. Growth that arrives after the relationship ends may be real but is functionally irrelevant to repair.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Is the partner showing change while still in the relationship, or only after loss? Post-loss growth, while valid personally, does not indicate the relationship was repairable.

decision_factors.factor: Length and depth of contact maintained post-breakup
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Gradual re-engagement (streaks → casual content → real conversation) appears in the successful case as a meaningful signal of reconnection willingness
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track whether contact is increasing in intimacy and frequency over weeks/months, or stalling at a superficial level

decision_factors.factor: Availability of practical social support
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Practical support (food, company, physical presence) addresses the body-in-shock phase where basic functioning is impaired; emotional support alone is insufficient in acute stages
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether you have people who can be physically present, bring food, or stay over — not just people to text

decision_factors.factor: History of tolerating lying or infidelity before the breakup
decision_factors.why_it_matters: People who stayed through repeated boundary violations report feeling depleted and having lost their sense of self, making post-breakup recovery significantly harder and increasing risk of accepting future mistreatment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Honestly inventory whether you normalized behaviors you knew were wrong in order to preserve the relationship

decision_factors.factor: Whether the avoidant's childhood trauma has been addressed
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Avoidant attachment is described as rooted in early experiences of having emotions shunned — without addressing the root cause, the pattern will resurface in every future relationship including any reconciliation attempt
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Has the person ever discussed their childhood emotional environment? Have they named the origin of their avoidance? Are they actively working on it?

decision_factors.factor: Presence of unresolved childhood or relational trauma in oneself
decision_factors.why_it_matters: One commenter with corroboration identifies that people who grew up in fear or chaos will unconsciously seek anxious or avoidant partners and feel suffocated by secure ones — this is a structural attractor, not a one-off choice
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask honestly whether you consistently attract or choose avoidant partners, or whether you end things with people who feel 'too stable' or 'too boring'

decision_factors.factor: How conflict-avoidant the partner is
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A highly conflict-avoidant partner will not self-report harassment; the harassing party exploits this silence to continue without consequence
decision_factors.how_to_assess: OP explicitly noted his girlfriend 'hates upsetting anyone' and 'avoids conflict' — this created the conditions for the harassment to persist undetected

decision_factors.factor: Jurisdiction's consent recording laws
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Whether evidence gathered via recorded conversation or third-party text is admissible for a police report depends on whether you are in a one-party or all-party consent jurisdiction.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check state/province law before attempting to gather admissions; Illinois is explicitly named as an all-party consent state in this post.

decision_factors.factor: Safety risk to self and child when partner is absent or indifferent
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Multiple commenters flagged that OP was alone with a 1-year-old while symptomatic and had no reliable partner to call for help — the partner's indifference creates a concrete safety gap, not just an emotional one
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: if I had a medical emergency while caring for my child and my partner was home, would they act? If the honest answer is 'probably not,' that is a safety risk requiring a concrete plan

decision_factors.factor: Quality of apology vs. magnitude of repair needed
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Flowers, coffee, and 'you are the most beautiful girl I know' address OP's ego but do not address the underlying value system that produced the comment — the community notes this distinction repeatedly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Does the apology acknowledge the specific harm (contemptuous attitude toward certain bodies) or only the surface event (saying it where she could hear)?

decision_factors.factor: Presence of a child in the household
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Child custody, the child witnessing violence, and the child's own trauma are compounding factors that both raise the stakes for leaving and raise the stakes for staying
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Has the child witnessed or been in proximity to violent incidents? Does the child ask about the absent parent in ways that suggest distress?

decision_factors.factor: Length of relationship relative to the duration of the deception
decision_factors.why_it_matters: When a 7-year relationship involves at least 4 months of parallel relationship plus sustained lies about family members over multiple years, the deception is not a recent aberration but a long-term pattern
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map the timeline: when did lying behaviors begin relative to relationship milestones (anniversaries, wedding planning, family events)?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the radicalized partner's family is supportive or antagonistic
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Family-of-origin support for the non-radicalized spouse reduces social isolation, may provide witness testimony, and signals the radicalized partner lacks a united support network to contest proceedings
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Has the partner's family reached out to express concern or support? Are they themselves radicalized?

decision_factors.factor: Children's inclusion in partner's care behaviors
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A live-in partner who excludes children from holiday acknowledgment signals limited buy-in to the full family unit, which is critical when marriage and children are being discussed
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe whether the partner spontaneously includes children in gift-giving, planning, or special occasions without prompting

decision_factors.factor: Whether the healthy partner has an independent support system and identity outside the relationship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A partner who has sacrificed their own hobbies, social life, and work-life balance to support a grieving fiancé will deplete faster and accumulate resentment that becomes irreversible
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether the healthy partner still has hobbies, friendships, and activities that are not mediated through the relationship

decision_factors.factor: Whether the partner acknowledged any wrongdoing after the confrontation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A partner who still maintains after the confrontation that locking a spouse out of a shared home is 'perfectly normal' is signaling no accountability or intent to change
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Did they apologize meaningfully, or did they reframe the confrontation as proof that the other partner is controlling?

decision_factors.factor: Whether a partner dismisses the other partner's interests as 'immature' or 'childish'
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Labeling a partner's interests as beneath them is a form of contempt — multiple commenters flagged this as a component of isolation and control, not mere preference difference
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Note whether dismissal is specific to one activity or applied broadly; whether it results in the partner abandoning the interest over time

decision_factors.factor: Presence of dependent children

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess ages, schooling, and which parent currently provides primary care

decision_factors.factor: Childhood trauma history of the person receiving caretaking
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The OP explicitly links the dynamic to unmet childhood needs — this means the emotional stakes of changing the dynamic are higher, and the person may resist change because the dependency feels like healing
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: does abandoning the caretaking feel like growth or like losing something emotionally necessary?

decision_factors.factor: Medical recovery timeline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The timing of separation matters when a person is post-surgical; leaving too abruptly without support infrastructure may trade one danger (harmful partner) for another (no care at all)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether physical recovery requires in-home care. If the partner is net-negative (more draining than helpful), leaving to a family member's home or other support environment may accelerate, not delay, recovery.

decision_factors.factor: Duration and consistency of the pattern versus isolated incidents
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A pattern spanning the entire relationship duration predicts future behavior more reliably than a single incident; in this case, virtually every fight across four years had the same root cause
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map conflicts across the relationship timeline — are they clustered around one trigger type, or varied? A single trigger type driving all conflict is a structural pattern, not a rough patch

decision_factors.factor: Projection of future emotional cost

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Visualize the next 2-3 years continuing on the current pattern — does that image produce relief or dread?
