diagnostic_questions.question: Is this the first breakup in this relationship, or have you broken up and reconciled before?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the breakup is an isolated event or part of a repeating cycle; repeated cycles with the same root cause predict the pattern will continue
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What specifically changed between the last reconciliation and this breakup that would prevent it from happening again?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: A first breakup may be a rough patch; assess root cause and both parties' willingness to change
diagnostic_questions._source: zhihu_分手后到底值不值得花时间精力去挽回.txt

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the ex's coldness strategic (suppressing feelings to discourage false hope) or genuine (emotional detachment is complete)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the ex still has feelings they are managing versus having genuinely moved on
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Strategic coldness: patience and low-pressure contact can create openings; ex may initiate once guard drops
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Genuine detachment: the window may have closed; continued pursuit risks harassment-level behavior
diagnostic_questions._source: zhihu_分手后还有挽回的可能吗.txt

diagnostic_questions.question: Over the past several weeks, has your dominant emotional state been happiness/security or sadness/suspicion/disappointment?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Net emotional valence is a more reliable signal than any single incident — chronic negative states indicate the relationship is extracting more than it is giving
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Investigate whether the negative state is relationship-generated or externally sourced (work stress, personal health, family) before attributing it to the relationship
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If baseline is positive with episodic conflict, the relationship likely has a repairable rough patch rather than a structural problem

diagnostic_questions.question: After the trust breach, is your partner monitoring you more intensely over time, or is the monitoring gradually decreasing?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the betrayed partner's threat system is recalibrating toward safety or escalating into a confirmation-bias spiral
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If monitoring is escalating despite consistent behavioral change: suggests a confirmation bias loop has formed — intervention may require direct conversation about the dynamic, not more compliance
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If monitoring is decreasing: trust repair is working — maintain consistency

diagnostic_questions.question: Do the problems you cite about your current partner also appear in the new option you are considering, or in your own relational patterns?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the problem is partner-specific (justifying leaving) or pattern-level (will follow you to the next relationship)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If the new option has the same problems: the issue is likely relational pattern, not this specific partner
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the new option appears problem-free: ask whether you know the new option well enough to make that assessment reliably

diagnostic_questions.question: Would you be making the same cost-benefit calculation about staying if you had not relocated or made significant life sacrifices for this relationship?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the decision to stay is driven by genuine belief in the relationship's future or by sunk cost and logistical dependency created by prior sacrifice.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What specifically about the relationship's future potential justifies staying, independent of what you've already invested?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The staying impulse is likely sunk-cost driven. The question becomes: what is the cost of continuing to invest in a depreciating asset versus absorbing the exit cost now?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you the primary earner and primary household manager? What happens to the household if you stop functioning?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The power asymmetry in the relationship — the person absorbing the most harm may also be the most economically vulnerable if they leave, but also the most structurally powerful if they act
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Consult a family law attorney now, before further financial deterioration — your position may be stronger than you think
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Assess what financial entanglement exists and who controls assets

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you and your ex articulate a concrete shared life plan — where you will live, when, what your respective life goals are, and how they are compatible?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the relationship has structural foundation beyond emotional attachment; relationships without shared trajectory tend to drift apart regardless of emotional intensity
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is that plan one both parties have explicitly agreed to, or is it an assumption one party holds?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Reconciliation without a shared plan may restore the relationship temporarily but leaves the underlying incompatibility unresolved
diagnostic_questions._source: zhihu_分手后到底值不值得花时间精力去挽回.txt

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the family opposition to the relationship about facts they don't know, or about values they hold that are unlikely to change?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether a 'win over the parents' strategy is viable or whether the couple faces a structural incompatibility with the family system
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Factual opposition: can be addressed with evidence, time, demonstrated behavior
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Values-based opposition: requires the partner to make an autonomous adult choice; no amount of impression management will substitute
diagnostic_questions._source: zhihu_分手后还有挽回的可能吗.txt

diagnostic_questions.question: When you make emotional repair gestures, does your partner seem slightly curious or warmed (even if they don't say so), or do they seem irritated and more withdrawn?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the repair approach matches the partner's attachment style — curiosity/warmth signals the approach is landing; irritation/withdrawal in an avoidant partner signals over-pursuit
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If warmth, even indirect: continue current approach, increase gradually
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If withdrawal increases: reduce intensity of pursuit immediately; switch to quieter, lower-pressure gestures

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your body telling you? Are you sleeping, eating, and feeling basically okay in this relationship, or are you chronically dysregulated?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the relationship is net-harmful at a physiological level, which is a more reliable signal than cognitive rationalizations in either direction
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If chronically dysregulated: treat somatic distress as a serious data point; do not override it with cognitive hope
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If basically okay physically: the distress may be situational and the relationship may be salvageable

industry_realities.common_belief: Common-law couples in Canada do not have the same property rights as married couples
industry_realities.actual_reality: In British Columbia specifically, unmarried couples who have lived together in a marriage-like relationship for at least 2 years have essentially the same statutory property-division rights as married couples under BC's Family Law Act; this is not true in Ontario, where no automatic property-division right exists for common-law couples regardless of duration
industry_realities.implication: A BC common-law partner past the 2-year mark must be advised using the same property-division framework as a married person; assuming no rights exist is factually incorrect under BC law

industry_realities.common_belief: Canadian and US custody determinations both use a 'best interests of the child' standard, so they function the same way
industry_realities.actual_reality: The Canadian Divorce Act imposes a codified, legally mandatory priority ordering — safety/security/well-being must be considered first under s.16(2) — whereas the US best interests standard (e.g., California) uses an unweighted multi-factor list without a statutory priority hierarchy
industry_realities.implication: In Canadian proceedings, a parent with documented safety concerns holds a structurally stronger legal position than the equivalent factor-balancing approach in many US jurisdictions would suggest; treating the two standards as equivalent misstates Canadian law

industry_realities.common_belief: You must wait until after the full 12-month separation period before you can file for divorce in Canada
industry_realities.actual_reality: The Divorce Act permits filing before the 12-month separation period is complete — the restriction is on finalization, not on filing
industry_realities.implication: A spouse can initiate the legal process early while the separation period runs, potentially reducing overall time to finalization after the 12 months elapse

industry_realities.common_belief: In Canada, common-law couples who have lived together for a significant period (e.g., 2+ years) automatically gain property-division rights similar to married couples
industry_realities.actual_reality: This is true in BC (2-year threshold) but explicitly not true in Ontario — Ontario has no duration threshold for common-law couples and provides zero automatic property-division rights regardless of how long the partners lived together
industry_realities.implication: Any person in a long-term common-law relationship in Ontario who has not signed a cohabitation agreement should understand they have no automatic claim to property held in their partner's name upon separation

industry_realities.common_belief: 'The best interests of the child' is a vague, judge-discretion standard with no defined criteria
industry_realities.actual_reality: In California, 'best interests of the child' is implemented through six concrete, enumerated factors under California Family Code §3011 — age and health, emotional ties, school/home/community ties, parental caregiving ability, family violence history, and regular/ongoing substance abuse
industry_realities.implication: Parents preparing for custody proceedings should evaluate their position on each of the six specific statutory factors, not approach the standard as an undefined discretionary inquiry

industry_realities.common_belief: You can file for divorce in California at any time once you decide to end the marriage
industry_realities.actual_reality: Filing requires one spouse to have lived in California for at least 6 months AND in the specific county for at least 3 months; neither condition can be waived by mutual agreement or immediate intent to file
industry_realities.implication: Anyone who has recently moved to California or to a new county must calculate the earliest eligible filing date before initiating divorce proceedings

industry_realities.common_belief: In a divorce, each spouse is entitled to half of everything regardless of which state they live in.
industry_realities.actual_reality: The 50/50 split is only the automatic rule in the nine community property states (and Alaska by opt-in agreement). The majority of US states use equitable distribution, where 'equitable' explicitly does not mean 'equal' — the split is determined by fairness factors including marriage length, income disparity, and non-financial contributions.
industry_realities.implication: A person divorcing in an equitable distribution state must actively identify and present the fairness factors that support their desired outcome rather than assuming a 50/50 result.

industry_realities.common_belief: Property-division rules for common-law couples are the same across Canada
industry_realities.actual_reality: Province determines the applicable rules entirely; BC grants automatic property-division rights after 2 years of marriage-like cohabitation, while Ontario grants no automatic statutory property division to common-law couples regardless of how long they lived together
industry_realities.implication: Any advisor or tool answering a Canadian unmarried person's question about property division on separation must obtain the province before applying any framework; a generic 'Canada' answer is not valid

industry_realities.common_belief: A parent who leaves an unsafe relationship may harm their custody outcome because courts value stability and continuity
industry_realities.actual_reality: Under Divorce Act s.16(2), documented safety concerns are the primary consideration — legally required to be weighed first — not a factor that stability or continuity arguments can simply outweigh
industry_realities.implication: Documented safety concerns in a Canadian parenting order proceeding reinforce rather than compete with a decision to leave an unsafe relationship; the statutory structure does not penalize a parent for prioritizing safety

industry_realities.common_belief: Proving adultery or cruelty in a Canadian divorce gives the accusing spouse legal or financial advantages over using the separation ground
industry_realities.actual_reality: The source identifies cruelty and adultery as rarely pursued precisely because the no-fault separation route exists and fault-based grounds require proof — no advantage from fault grounds is stated
industry_realities.implication: In the absence of a specific strategic reason, the separation ground is the standard path; pursuing fault grounds introduces evidentiary complexity without a stated benefit

industry_realities.common_belief: Dividing property in Ontario on marriage breakdown means physically splitting each asset 50/50
industry_realities.actual_reality: Ontario uses an equalization payment system, not a physical 50/50 asset split — each spouse keeps their own property but the spouse who accumulated more net family property during the marriage pays half the difference in NFP to the other spouse
industry_realities.implication: Spouses should focus on accurately calculating net family property figures rather than assuming each individual asset will be divided in half

industry_realities.common_belief: Family violence and substance abuse are general background factors that courts consider alongside everything else
industry_realities.actual_reality: Under California Family Code §3011, family violence history and regular and ongoing substance abuse are explicitly enumerated statutory factors — they are mandatory considerations, not discretionary background context
industry_realities.implication: Documentation of family violence or substance abuse has direct legal significance in custody proceedings, not merely in the relationship-repair or safety decision

industry_realities.common_belief: No-fault divorce means there are no procedural requirements or waiting periods
industry_realities.actual_reality: No-fault eliminates the requirement to prove wrongdoing and removes the need for spousal consent, but residency requirements (6 months state, 3 months county) are separate procedural thresholds that remain fully in effect
industry_realities.implication: Spouses must satisfy both residency thresholds regardless of how clear-cut or uncontested the no-fault grounds are

industry_realities.common_belief: Whoever's name is on the asset owns it in a community property state.
industry_realities.actual_reality: In community property states, titling is irrelevant to ownership — both spouses own all assets acquired during the marriage equally 50/50, regardless of whose name appears on the title or who earned the income used to purchase the asset.
industry_realities.implication: A spouse cannot protect an asset from division in a community property state simply by keeping it in their own name.

industry_realities.common_belief: Before 2013, unmarried BC couples had the same property rights they have today
industry_realities.actual_reality: Before 2013, unmarried couples in BC had no statutory right to court-ordered property division at all; the current rights were created by legislative reform reflecting the increasing prevalence of common-law families
industry_realities.implication: Advice or case outcomes from before 2013 in BC are not reliable precedent for current statutory rights; the legal landscape changed materially with the Family Law Act reform

industry_realities.common_belief: Courts can only consider factors explicitly listed in the Divorce Act when determining best interests
industry_realities.actual_reality: The Divorce Act explicitly designates its factor list as non-exhaustive — courts may consider case-specific factors not enumerated in the statute
industry_realities.implication: Parties should not assume that a relevant circumstance is legally irrelevant simply because it does not appear on the statutory list

industry_realities.common_belief: Post-divorce child arrangements in Canada are still governed by 'custody and access' terminology
industry_realities.actual_reality: Effective March 1, 2021, the Divorce Act replaced 'custody and access' with 'parenting arrangements' — the old terminology is no longer the operative legal framework
industry_realities.implication: Any divorce proceedings, agreements, or legal documents referencing child arrangements must use 'parenting arrangements' language to conform to the current Act

industry_realities.common_belief: A spouse who owned the family home before marriage, or received it as a gift or inheritance, can exclude that value from the equalization calculation just like other pre-marriage or inherited assets
industry_realities.actual_reality: Ontario law explicitly carves out the matrimonial home from the standard exclusions — the full value of the family home is always included in the equalization calculation regardless of how or when it was acquired
industry_realities.implication: A spouse who brought a home into the marriage or inherited it during the marriage cannot protect that value from equalization the way they could protect, for example, an inherited bank account

industry_realities.common_belief: The 'best interests of the child' factors are the same across all US states
industry_realities.actual_reality: The source explicitly states that while all US states use the 'best interests of the child' standard, 'the specific enumerated factors vary by state' — California's six-factor list under §3011 is that state's implementation, not a universal list
industry_realities.implication: Parents in states other than California must identify their state's specific enumerated factors rather than assuming California's §3011 factors apply

industry_realities.common_belief: California's divorce residency rules represent the national standard
industry_realities.actual_reality: The official source explicitly states that residency windows vary by state, commonly ranging from 3 to 12 months depending on the state, and that terminology also varies ('dissolution of marriage' vs. 'divorce')
industry_realities.implication: Spouses who have moved from California to another state must research that specific state's residency requirement rather than assuming California's 6-month/3-month thresholds apply

industry_realities.common_belief: Alaska is a community property state.
industry_realities.actual_reality: Alaska allows community property treatment only as an opt-in — couples must affirmatively elect it by agreement. Without such an agreement, Alaska uses equitable distribution.
industry_realities.implication: A spouse in Alaska cannot assume community property protections apply; the existence of a written opt-in agreement must be verified.

industry_realities.common_belief: Either spouse can file for divorce in Canada regardless of where they currently live
industry_realities.actual_reality: At least one spouse must have resided in a Canadian province or territory for at least one year; if neither spouse meets this requirement, the federal Divorce Act is unavailable
industry_realities.implication: Spouses who have both relocated outside Canada must verify residency eligibility before assuming the Divorce Act applies to their situation

industry_realities.common_belief: A separated spouse always has 6 years to bring an equalization claim
industry_realities.actual_reality: The limitation period is the earlier of 6 years from separation OR 2 years from finalized divorce — if the divorce is finalized, the 2-year post-divorce clock may expire well before the 6-year separation clock, eliminating the right to claim
industry_realities.implication: Spouses should not assume the 6-year period applies as a floor; finalizing a divorce quickly can inadvertently reduce the available window for an equalization claim to 2 years from the divorce date

industry_realities.common_belief: Decisions about leaving a relationship with children are primarily an adult emotional and financial calculus
industry_realities.actual_reality: The source states that 'best interests of the child' is 'the literal legal standard a court applies, built from concrete, checkable factors' — the adult relationship history and grievances are not the court's framework; the six §3011 factors are
industry_realities.implication: Adults with children must evaluate the custody implications of leaving through the lens of the six statutory factors, not only through the lens of the adult relationship breakdown

industry_realities.common_belief: The decision to leave a relationship and the ability to file for divorce are the same question
industry_realities.actual_reality: The official source explicitly identifies these as two separate axes: 'A user asking should I leave and a user asking how do I actually leave, given I just moved states are asking different questions that require different information'
industry_realities.implication: Advisors and individuals must address emotional/repairability diagnosis and legal/procedural eligibility as distinct inquiries, not a single combined question

industry_realities.common_belief: Gifts and inheritances received during the marriage are shared marital property subject to division.
industry_realities.actual_reality: Under community property rules, property received individually as a gift or inheritance is classified as separate property and is generally excluded from the marital estate subject to division.
industry_realities.implication: A spouse who received a significant inheritance or gift during the marriage should document it as separate property to preserve its exclusion from division.

industry_realities.common_belief: A moment of sudden clarity about whether to stay or leave is a reliable signal — especially if it feels unusually calm or certain
industry_realities.actual_reality: For insecurely attached individuals, felt certainty is generated by the attachment system responding to momentary interpersonal cues — the clarity is a product of the current attachment state, not an independent evaluation of the relationship's actual trajectory
industry_realities.implication: Felt certainty should be treated as one data point requiring triangulation against pattern evidence from multiple emotional states, not as the decision itself

industry_realities.common_belief: Abuse is identifiable primarily by physical violence, and non-physical behaviors only count if they are frequent or severe
industry_realities.actual_reality: The canonical clinical and hotline framework explicitly includes non-physical behaviors (jealousy, isolation, financial control, intimidation, substance pressure, decision control) and sets the threshold at one or two present behaviors regardless of severity or frequency
industry_realities.implication: Any relationship-decision screening process must include a prior gate for the full 12-item list before applying a repairability framework; anchoring to physical harm alone will systematically miss cases that meet the abuse threshold

industry_realities.common_belief: Conflict itself is the problem — healthy relationships have little or no fighting
industry_realities.actual_reality: Gottman's longitudinal research shows all relationships have conflict; the differentiating variable is not whether conflict occurs but whether repair attempts consistently succeed afterward
industry_realities.implication: Evaluating a relationship by how much it fights is the wrong diagnostic; couples should instead assess the quality and success rate of their repair cycles

industry_realities.common_belief: Trust after infidelity rebuilds gradually on its own as time passes and the affair recedes into the past
industry_realities.actual_reality: The research identifies trust rebuilding as requiring conscious, sustained, active effort from both partners — time without effort does not produce the outcome; the mechanism is behavioral consistency, not elapsed calendar time
industry_realities.implication: Couples who are 'waiting it out' without a structured behavioral process are likely not rebuilding trust; the passage of time is neither necessary nor sufficient

industry_realities.common_belief: If a partner pulls away when you are being warm and open, they are signaling that they do not want closeness with you specifically or do not value the relationship
industry_realities.actual_reality: Avoidant deactivating strategies produce diminished warmth specifically in response to perceived partner warmth — the withdrawal is a triggered protective response, meaning increased partner warmth can actually intensify the withdrawal
industry_realities.implication: Escalating warmth or emotional intensity toward an avoidantly attached partner as a repair strategy will likely produce the opposite of the intended effect — the mechanism needs to be addressed, not overridden by volume

industry_realities.common_belief: The hotline is only reachable by phone and is only for people in immediate physical danger
industry_realities.actual_reality: The hotline offers phone (1-800-799-SAFE), text (START to 88788), and live chat at thehotline.org, and also provides proactive safety planning tools — not only crisis response
industry_realities.implication: Referrals should always include all three contact modes and mention the Plan for Safety tools, because the person's safest access method and urgency level will vary

industry_realities.common_belief: If a couple is still together and not miserable, the relationship is on a stable trajectory
industry_realities.actual_reality: A marriage can statistically survive the Four Horsemen — meaning it does not end in divorce — while remaining chronically unhappy; survival and health are distinct outcomes
industry_realities.implication: Remaining together is not sufficient evidence of repairability; the presence of contempt and failed repair attempts must be assessed independently of whether the couple has separated

industry_realities.common_belief: Progress in trust rebuilding should feel steady and cumulative — if it feels like you're going backward, something is wrong
industry_realities.actual_reality: The literature explicitly identifies the process as non-linear; setbacks are expected features of the process, not evidence it has broken down
industry_realities.implication: Evaluating the health of a repair process by whether it feels emotionally smooth will produce false negatives; the correct evaluation criterion is whether the behavioral commitments remain intact through the setbacks

industry_realities.common_belief: Relationship quality assessments made during therapy or journaling are more accurate because the person is being reflective
industry_realities.actual_reality: If reflection is happening primarily during or immediately after conflict or a triggering interaction, the assessment is still contaminated by the active attachment state — the medium of reflection does not neutralize the state-dependent distortion
industry_realities.implication: Assessments collected only during distress periods systematically overrepresent perceived problems; accurate diagnosis requires sampling across multiple emotional states including genuine calm

industry_realities.common_belief: A relationship-decision framework can be applied universally to any couple considering staying, repairing, or leaving
industry_realities.actual_reality: The standard repairability diagnostic is explicitly not appropriate when abuse indicators are present; applying it in that context risks reframing abuse as a mutual communication or compatibility problem
industry_realities.implication: Abuse screening must function as a hard prerequisite gate — not a weighted factor — before any repairability or trust-repair conversation begins

industry_realities.common_belief: Contempt is one of several equally serious communication problems to address
industry_realities.actual_reality: Gottman's research identifies contempt as the single greatest predictor of divorce — qualitatively different in predictive power from the other three Horsemen
industry_realities.implication: In any repair effort, eliminating contempt deserves disproportionate attention; progress on the other three Horsemen without addressing contempt leaves the most dangerous factor in place

industry_realities.common_belief: The primary indicator that trust is rebuilding is the betrayed partner's increasing emotional sense of security
industry_realities.actual_reality: The research points to observable behavioral indicators on the involved partner's side — cessation of contact, voluntary transparency, proactive disclosure of accidental contact, non-defensiveness in hard conversations — as the evidence base for repair, not the betrayed partner's emotional state alone
industry_realities.implication: Emotional security can be manufactured by avoidance, denial, or fatigue-driven acceptance; behavioral evidence is harder to fake and provides a more reliable diagnostic

industry_realities.common_belief: Inconsistent behavior from a partner — sometimes warm, sometimes cold — is evidence that the relationship is unstable or that the partner is ambivalent
industry_realities.actual_reality: Anxious attachment produces behavioral inconsistency that is internally generated — the anxiously attached person may respond to identical partner behavior with warmth on one occasion and withdrawal on another, making the inconsistency a property of the attachment system, not the relationship
industry_realities.implication: Before attributing relationship instability to the dynamic between two people, identify whether one person's responses are consistent with hyperactivating attachment patterns that would produce the observed variability independently

industry_realities.common_belief: Taking a break from a heated argument automatically helps the situation
industry_realities.actual_reality: A break only helps if it is used for genuine physiological self-soothing; ruminating on grievances during the break — 'righteous indignation' — fails to lower heart rate and can make the subsequent conversation worse
industry_realities.implication: Couples need to actively structure what happens during timeouts, not just agree to take them; the quality of the break determines whether it functions as a repair mechanism

industry_realities.common_belief: Monitoring tools like shared phone access are a sign the relationship is damaged and not truly repaired
industry_realities.actual_reality: The research treats concrete accountability measures as legitimate trust-building actions during the repair period, not as indicators of ongoing dysfunction — the COVID-19 period's constraints produced monitored communication as a natural accountability structure and this was studied as a positive feature
industry_realities.implication: Temporary structured accountability is a clinically recognized part of the repair process, not a sign of failure; the question is whether it remains time-limited and scaffolding rather than becoming permanent control

industry_realities.common_belief: Divorce prediction from communication patterns requires extensive professional observation
industry_realities.actual_reality: Gottman's methods predicted divorce with over 90% accuracy using observable variables — interaction ratio, presence of the Four Horsemen, and physiological measures — making this a practically usable diagnostic framework, not just a research tool
industry_realities.implication: Individuals can apply a structured version of this framework to their own relationship rather than relying solely on subjective feelings of happiness or unhappiness

industry_realities.common_belief: Ending a relationship that had good years means those years were wasted or the relationship was a failure
industry_realities.actual_reality: Past validity and current functionality are independent variables — a relationship can have been genuinely valuable and also no longer be meeting needs; ending it is a needs assessment, not a verdict on the past
industry_realities.implication: Stay-or-leave decisions made through the past-value frame will systematically produce over-staying; the frame itself needs to be named and dismantled before the decision can be made clearly

industry_realities.common_belief: Feeling certain you want to leave a relationship is a reliable signal that the relationship is genuinely not working
industry_realities.actual_reality: For avoidantly attached individuals, strong felt certainty about wanting to leave can be entirely manufactured by the attachment system's defensive response to intimacy — the feeling is real but its cause is the anxiety of closeness, not genuine incompatibility
industry_realities.implication: Felt certainty about leaving must be stress-tested against its timing and triggers before it is treated as evidence about the relationship's actual state, particularly for people with avoidant attachment patterns

industry_realities.common_belief: If a relationship feels broken, it is broken and should be exited
industry_realities.actual_reality: Relationships that feel broken are sometimes depleted — structurally intact but running on empty due to external stressors — and the subjective feeling of brokenness cannot reliably distinguish the two without a structured diagnostic
industry_realities.implication: Apply a structured diagnostic before using felt sense as the primary decision input; the feeling of brokenness is data, not a conclusion

industry_realities.common_belief: If someone can see the signs pointing toward leaving (ongoing anxiety, no progress, unresolved withdrawal), the decision is straightforward
industry_realities.actual_reality: Outcome-level signs are necessary but not sufficient — they can be produced by attachment mechanisms that are independent of the relationship's repair potential, and acting on them without checking the mechanism layer misfires on anxious-avoidant couples specifically
industry_realities.implication: Practitioners and individuals need a two-layer diagnostic: outcome-level (has enough time passed with no visible improvement) and mechanism-level (is the apparent no-improvement actually an attachment cycle artifact)

industry_realities.common_belief: If you are noticing more and more things wrong with your partner, that is evidence your incompatibility is becoming clearer over time
industry_realities.actual_reality: Avoidant deactivating strategies specifically manifest as manufacturing petty reasons to exit — noticing more flaws is a known symptom of proximity anxiety, not necessarily of genuine incompatibility becoming apparent
industry_realities.implication: An inventory of partner flaws needs to be evaluated for timing and triviality before being used as relationship-exit evidence; a sudden increase in noticed flaws correlating with increased closeness should be treated as a red flag about the observer's attachment state, not about the partner

industry_realities.common_belief: Talking through problems is the core mechanism of relationship repair
industry_realities.actual_reality: Substantive problem-solving requires cognitive access that is only available after emotional safety and connection have been established; problem-solving conversations held without those conditions in place will fail regardless of the quality of the proposed solution
industry_realities.implication: Sequence repair conversations in the correct order — safety first, then connection, then cognitive work, then problem-solving — rather than leading with the substantive issue

industry_realities.common_belief: Mutual willingness to change is something you can determine by asking each partner directly
industry_realities.actual_reality: Apparent unwillingness may be avoidant deactivation — a state-dependent shutdown under emotional load — rather than a stable trait; the same partner may show genuine willingness in lower-stakes conditions
industry_realities.implication: Assess willingness across conditions, not in a single high-stakes moment; a partner who appears unwilling during conflict but engages in calm reflection may be deactivating, not refusing

industry_realities.common_belief: An anxious partner pushing for more closeness when their partner withdraws is a reasonable attempt to repair the relationship
industry_realities.actual_reality: In an anxious-avoidant dynamic, the pushing behavior is the direct trigger for intensified avoidant withdrawal — the repair attempt actively worsens the symptom it is trying to address, creating an escalating cycle where neither partner's assessment of the relationship reflects its actual state
industry_realities.implication: Anxious partners in this dynamic need to understand that reducing pursuit — counterintuitive as it feels — is more likely to create conditions where the avoidant partner can accurately assess their own feelings than escalating bids for closeness

industry_realities.common_belief: Both people trying hard is sufficient for a relationship to be repaired
industry_realities.actual_reality: Effort is necessary but not sufficient; the presence of abuse, contempt, fundamental values incompatibility, or unilateral willingness are conditions that effort cannot overcome, and continuing to try in their presence is not repair but delay
industry_realities.implication: Assess structural conditions — the 'let go' criteria — before investing further in effort-based repair; if any hard condition is present, additional effort should not be the next step

industry_realities.common_belief: Conflict is a sign that a relationship is in serious trouble
industry_realities.actual_reality: Conflict and contempt are categorically different; conflict is a normal feature of relationships and does not predict failure, while contempt — which involves fundamental disrespect or disgust directed at the person — specifically predicts failure
industry_realities.implication: Evaluate conflict for the presence of contempt rather than treating conflict presence or intensity as the relevant variable

industry_realities.common_belief: If there was no cheating or abuse, the relationship wasn't seriously damaged and can be recovered with time
industry_realities.actual_reality: Consistent emotional neglect — not showing up, not listening, not providing reassurance — causes damage that is 'quieter and sometimes deeper' than acute harm. Multiple commenters recognized this pattern in their own relationships as the actual cause of breakdown.
industry_realities.implication: Benchmarking your behavior against the worst-case threshold (abuse, infidelity) is not a valid measure of whether you are meeting a partner's needs. Absence of harm is not presence of care.

industry_realities.common_belief: Fighting for someone you love shows strength and increases the chance they return
industry_realities.actual_reality: When you are the dumpee, direct pursuit typically reduces your perceived value and confirms the dumper's decision; withdrawal and demonstrated self-sufficiency are more effective signals
industry_realities.implication: Reframe 'fighting for them' as investing in yourself visibly, not as direct persuasion or persistent contact

industry_realities.common_belief: Time heals all wounds — you just need to wait it out
industry_realities.actual_reality: Time is a necessary but not sufficient condition; healing requires active emotional engagement during that time. Passive waiting without processing can leave someone stuck indefinitely
industry_realities.implication: People who believe waiting is enough will under-invest in the active work (processing, graduated exposure, identity reconstruction) and be surprised when years pass without resolution

industry_realities.common_belief: When someone says you are their soulmate, their person, or that they want to spend their life with you, this reflects a stable and evaluated commitment
industry_realities.actual_reality: As multiple commenters observed, people who use the strongest romantic language early in relationships are often 'high on fantasy fumes' — they sincerely feel it in the moment but are expressing an idealized projection, not a tested commitment. The language predicts the intensity of the infatuation phase, not the durability of the bond
industry_realities.implication: Recipients of such declarations should not build long-term emotional infrastructure (shared plans, identity merger, symbolic commitments like promise rings) on verbal intensity alone — behavioral consistency across time and adversity is the more reliable signal

industry_realities.common_belief: Time alone heals a breakup — you just need to wait it out
industry_realities.actual_reality: Time is necessary but not sufficient; multiple experienced commenters emphasized that healing requires active behavioral change — making new friends, pursuing old passions, trying new experiences — not passive waiting
industry_realities.implication: People who wait passively for healing while avoiding action are likely to remain stuck significantly longer than those who initiate behavioral changes even before they feel ready

industry_realities.common_belief: Standard recovery tools — no contact, gym, therapy, music — will reliably produce healing within a predictable timeframe
industry_realities.actual_reality: For some people, especially those who had genuinely good relationships that ended abruptly, these tools do not produce noticeable relief even after 8 months; the quality and nature of the relationship matters as much as the coping strategy
industry_realities.implication: People should not measure recovery progress against a standard timeline or assume tool failure means personal failure; the grief for an unexpectedly lost good relationship may require a different intervention than grief for a toxic one

industry_realities.common_belief: If the relationship was healthy, there must be a real reason for the breakup that the other person isn't sharing
industry_realities.actual_reality: People can and do grow apart with no single identifiable cause — diverging life trajectories, changing identities, or quiet emotional drift can end a structurally healthy relationship without any specific triggering event
industry_realities.implication: Demanding a 'real reason' from an ex who says they grew apart may be a way of avoiding accepting that love and health are not sufficient conditions for a relationship to continue

industry_realities.common_belief: If you improve yourself enough during no-contact, your ex will come back
industry_realities.actual_reality: Self-improvement during no-contact increases your overall attractiveness and emotional stability, but it does not override an ex's decision if their reason for leaving was not the behavior you improved — particularly if they left for another person
industry_realities.implication: Frame self-improvement as insurance for your own future, not as a guaranteed reconciliation mechanism; evaluate whether the ex's stated reason and actual reason align before investing months of effort into a specific outcome

industry_realities.common_belief: Avoidant people don't care and have simply moved on — their emotional composure after a breakup proves they were never really invested
industry_realities.actual_reality: Avoidants are described by a self-identified avoidant as often among the most self-aware people in a relationship — they are aware of their feelings, including regret, but have a deep-seated block against expressing them, rooted in early experiences of having emotional expression punished
industry_realities.implication: Interpreting avoidant silence as indifference leads to premature closure-seeking or self-blame; the silence is a coping mechanism, not a verdict on the relationship's worth

industry_realities.common_belief: If your ex seems fine and has moved on quickly, it means they didn't care as much as you did
industry_realities.actual_reality: People who initiate breakups have a head start on emotional processing — they began grieving the relationship before it ended; visible recovery speed reflects timing, not depth of feeling or comparative worth
industry_realities.implication: Benchmarking your healing against theirs is a false comparison that produces unnecessary pain and bad decisions (like rushing into a rebound to keep up)

industry_realities.common_belief: When someone gives an emotional, tearful, morally grounded reason for a breakup, they are being honest even if the outcome is painful
industry_realities.actual_reality: Tears and moral framing during a breakup do not correlate with honesty — they can be the delivery mechanism for a false explanation that protects the leaver from accountability while giving the abandoned partner a story they can process without anger
industry_realities.implication: Abandoned partners should treat emotionally dramatic breakup explanations with the same scrutiny as any other claim, and look to behavior in the weeks following as the more reliable signal

industry_realities.common_belief: If you were a good partner, the person who left will eventually realize their mistake and come back
industry_realities.actual_reality: Being a good partner is not sufficient to override a partner's decision to leave — the decision to leave is about their internal state and choices, not a ledger of your contributions
industry_realities.implication: Waiting for recognition of your value as a retention strategy is not a strategy — it is grief dressed as hope

industry_realities.common_belief: Protecting a child from painful truths about their origins is an act of love that prevents harm
industry_realities.actual_reality: According to a commenter with professional adoption work experience, post-2000 adoption counseling guidance explicitly advises against secret parentage arrangements — early, age-appropriate disclosure is considered less harmful than deferred disclosure because secrets are psychologically 'felt' even when not consciously known
industry_realities.implication: Families considering whether to disclose should understand that delay does not eliminate harm — it transfers it, often to a worse moment and in a less controlled form

industry_realities.common_belief: If a friend ghosts you after you've done something that affected them, the problem is between you and the friend and can be solved by reaching out more
industry_realities.actual_reality: When a controlling or abusive partner is involved, the friend's silence is often a protective act — both for herself and for the OP. The real audience for every message OP sends is the partner, not the friend. More messages can make things worse for the friend.
industry_realities.implication: Before escalating direct outreach, assess the friend's home situation. If there are warning signs of control, route any contact through a mutual friend and pull back on direct messaging.

industry_realities.common_belief: Being on a shared lease means you cannot leave a relationship without the other person's agreement or until the lease ends.
industry_realities.actual_reality: Lease entanglement complicates but does not prevent exit. Options include subletting, lease buyout negotiation with the landlord, one party taking over the lease, or — in cases involving documented abuse — early termination protections that exist in many US states and Canadian provinces.
industry_realities.implication: People who believe they are trapped by a lease delay safety planning that should begin immediately when a volatile partner is present.

industry_realities.common_belief: Family loyalty means giving a parent or sibling repeated chances before taking serious action
industry_realities.actual_reality: Multiple experienced commenters — including those who went NC with parents — reported that repeated chances without enforced consequences trained the family member that the behavior had no real cost
industry_realities.implication: The first clearly-communicated consequence with follow-through is more effective and kinder in the long run than many warnings without action

industry_realities.common_belief: Reproductive coercion (tampering with birth control) is a relationship betrayal that can potentially be worked through with communication and couples therapy.
industry_realities.actual_reality: Multiple informed commenters categorized it unambiguously as sexual assault and a crime, not a relationship problem. The consensus framing was that it places the perpetrator outside the category of 'partner who made a mistake' entirely.
industry_realities.implication: Victims should orient toward legal reporting and safety planning, not relationship repair frameworks — applying a repair lens to this situation actively delays protective action.

industry_realities.common_belief: A partner who does their share of housework and doesn't complain about chores has fundamentally improved the relationship
industry_realities.actual_reality: Task-sharing is a necessary but not sufficient condition for a healthy relationship — it removes a category of grievance but does not create emotional attunement or care capacity, which only surfaces under stress
industry_realities.implication: Using chore equity as the primary metric for 'things are better' leaves empathy deficits undetected until a crisis event forces them into view

industry_realities.common_belief: A partner staying calm, loving, and physically present after causing harm is evidence they meant no harm
industry_realities.actual_reality: Experienced commenters note this is a documented feature of certain control dynamics — staying present and acting loving after triggering a destabilizing event (like a police visit) is tactically useful: it positions the perpetrator as the stable, caring one while the victim is distressed, and can be used to frame the victim as overreacting
industry_realities.implication: Post-incident loving behavior should be evaluated in context of the full sequence, not treated as exculpatory on its own

industry_realities.common_belief: Leaving a shared apartment and stopping contact is sufficient to end a cohabiting relationship
industry_realities.actual_reality: In registered domestic partnerships (California and other states), the legal relationship persists until a formal termination form is filed with the county. Insurance coverage, potential property claims, and other legal entitlements continue until affirmative dissolution steps are completed.
industry_realities.implication: Someone who walks out without filing termination paperwork may remain legally linked to their ex for months, exposing them to continued financial and legal entanglement

industry_realities.common_belief: Inheritance automatically affects child support obligations, so an ex has a legitimate interest in knowing about it
industry_realities.actual_reality: Inheritance is not a marital asset and is not subject to child support calculations as long as it is kept separate — the ex has no legal entitlement to the information and no legal claim on the funds
industry_realities.implication: The ex's anger and demands are not legally grounded; OP does not need to disclose inheritance details and the breach caused real harm with no legitimate justification

industry_realities.common_belief: People are allowed to have physical types, and having a preference for fit people is morally neutral
industry_realities.actual_reality: Having a physical preference is neutral; expressing contempt and using dehumanizing language about people who don't meet that preference is a character issue, not a preference issue — multiple comments distinguish between these clearly
industry_realities.implication: OP should not be asking whether it's okay that her boyfriend has a type, but whether it's okay that he responds to people outside his type with visible disgust and dehumanizing language

industry_realities.common_belief: A partner who 'just wants to see an ultrasound' before you decide is asking for a neutral informational step
industry_realities.actual_reality: Community members with pattern recognition flagged the ultrasound request as a documented bonding-induction tactic used to erode a firm decision against continuing a pregnancy
industry_realities.implication: Agreeing to delay for an ultrasound when you have already made a clear decision should be recognized as a risk to that decision, not a neutral compromise

industry_realities.common_belief: If the relationship has good moments and the partner isn't 'always' abusive, the relationship is probably repairable with better communication
industry_realities.actual_reality: The presence of a honeymoon or affectionate phase is a feature of abusive relationship cycles, not evidence against abuse; multiple mental health professionals in the thread confirmed that intermittent reinforcement (alternating warmth and violence) is precisely the mechanism that makes abusive relationships harder to leave, not evidence of repairability
industry_realities.implication: Evaluating a relationship's health based on its best moments is the wrong frame; the diagnostic question is what happens when conflict arises or when the victim sets a boundary

industry_realities.common_belief: A partner's family can be neutral arbiters who will hold them accountable when shown evidence of cheating
industry_realities.actual_reality: The family's primary loyalty is to their family member; when shown receipts, the sister's first response was hostility toward OP, and her primary distress was about her friend (the affair partner) being deceived by the cheater — not about OP's 7 years
industry_realities.implication: Sharing evidence with a cheater's family may produce drama and secondary information, but it rarely produces the accountability the betrayed partner hopes for; manage expectations accordingly

industry_realities.common_belief: Family courts strongly prefer joint custody arrangements, making sole custody very difficult to obtain
industry_realities.actual_reality: While joint custody is the baseline preference, documented domestic violence — especially incidents that result in police contact and arrest — significantly shifts the calculus toward sole custody for the non-violent parent; OP's lawyer confirmed the DV incident materially strengthened their position
industry_realities.implication: Non-radicalized parents should not assume sole custody is out of reach; they should focus on building a documented record rather than accepting joint custody as inevitable

industry_realities.common_belief: Apologizing and feeling bad in the moment is sufficient repair after a significant omission like this
industry_realities.actual_reality: Multiple commenters noted that reactive remorse (hugging, apologizing after being caught) is not the same as proactive thoughtfulness; the apology does not address the underlying deprioritization
industry_realities.implication: Accept an apology as a starting point but require behavioral change — specifically, proactive planning — before updating your assessment of the partner's investment level

industry_realities.common_belief: If someone is going to therapy, they are doing the work and recovery should be visible within a year
industry_realities.actual_reality: Attending therapy and engaging with therapy are entirely different things; a grieving person who attends therapy cynically and dismisses all input is receiving no therapeutic benefit, and the form of compliance provides false reassurance to both partners
industry_realities.implication: The healthy partner should assess the quality of therapeutic engagement, not just its presence, when evaluating whether progress is occurring

industry_realities.common_belief: Adding a lock to a home office to protect valuables from a toddler is a normal, reasonable thing to do
industry_realities.actual_reality: Child-proofing solutions exist (specific toddler-resistant handles, safety knobs) that allow adult access while blocking children; an external padlock with a missing key is not a child-proofing solution — it is a spousal exclusion mechanism
industry_realities.implication: The stated justification for the lock should have been evaluated against available alternatives; the choice of a padlock specifically is diagnostic of intent

industry_realities.common_belief: Writing things down in notes is the reliable fix for a bad memory
industry_realities.actual_reality: For people with ADHD or executive function challenges, note-taking has high friction and gets procrastinated — photos taken immediately at the hiding spot are more reliable because they require less cognitive overhead
industry_realities.implication: The right tool depends on the person's specific failure mode; prescribing 'just write it down' without accounting for why that fails misses the actual problem

industry_realities.common_belief: Couples counseling will surface and address all the significant problems in the relationship if you attend consistently
industry_realities.actual_reality: Couples counseling only addresses what is explicitly named in the room — a partner who is controlling may use the counseling sessions to appear engaged while the specific behaviors driving the problem are never brought in directly
industry_realities.implication: Attending couples counseling while leaving the specific behavioral patterns unnamed provides a false sense of progress; individual therapy to identify and name the behaviors is a necessary prerequisite

industry_realities.common_belief: A partner who identifies as polyamorous is making an honest identity disclosure that deserves the same respect as any other identity
industry_realities.actual_reality: Identity framing can be sincere or it can be deployed instrumentally to preempt objection — the distinction is revealed by behavioral evidence (asymmetric permission, pre-existing target, refusal to honor any limits) not by the label itself
industry_realities.implication: The identity claim should not short-circuit normal relationship evaluation; behavior, timing, and reciprocity are still the relevant signals

industry_realities.common_belief: A partner who does everything for you is an unambiguous good — friends' envy confirms this
industry_realities.actual_reality: Total caretaking without active maintenance of individual capability produces functional dependency; the person who benefits can lose skills, confidence, and identity coherence even while materially comfortable
industry_realities.implication: Healthy partnership requires deliberate preservation of individual competence — accepting all support without maintaining any self-reliance is a structural risk even in loving relationships

industry_realities.common_belief: If you just communicate your needs clearly enough, a partner will understand and step up
industry_realities.actual_reality: Multiple commenters noted that OP had communicated her needs explicitly and repeatedly — she asked him to stay home, told him she was scared, asked for help with laundry weeks in advance. Clarity of communication was not the variable. The partner's willingness to respond was.
industry_realities.implication: When a partner has been given clear, direct, explicit requests and consistently fails to act, the problem is not communication — it is motivation or character. Reframing it as a communication problem extends the relationship at the cost of the person in need.

industry_realities.common_belief: Having a diagnosed mental health condition means a person cannot be held responsible for behaviors that stem from that condition
industry_realities.actual_reality: Having a diagnosis explains the origin of a behavior but does not transfer responsibility for managing it to the partner; the person with the condition is responsible for seeking and sustaining treatment
industry_realities.implication: A partner should not accept chronic mistreatment because a clinical label has been attached to the behavior; the label changes the cause, not the impact or the responsibility

industry_realities.common_belief: The affair partner who 'wins' the cheating spouse gets a prize — they get the person, the relationship, and some version of a normal life
industry_realities.actual_reality: The relationship built on the affair carries the reputational damage of its origins into every professional and social context; in this case, both parties lost their teaching careers, had to relocate to avoid social ostracism, and found themselves excluded from the social networks they wanted to remain part of
industry_realities.implication: The betrayed partner who fears the affair partner 'won' should assess the full downstream picture — what the relationship built on betrayal actually costs both parties over time, not just at the point of discovery

industry_realities.common_belief: A partner who apologizes and says they 'didn't mean it' after a blow-up is showing genuine remorse and the relationship can recover
industry_realities.actual_reality: Multiple experienced commenters noted that rapid post-conflict retractions are a predictable move in a manipulation cycle — the apology addresses the words, not the behavior, and the underlying dynamic remains unchanged
industry_realities.implication: Evaluate apologies by whether they name the specific harm and produce observable behavioral change — not by whether they reduce your immediate distress

industry_realities.common_belief: Blocking a controlling ex on major social media (Instagram, Facebook, Twitter) is sufficient to prevent digital tracking
industry_realities.actual_reality: Professional platforms (LinkedIn), public records databases, data broker aggregator sites, and mutual social connections all remain as active location and contact vectors even after social media blocking
industry_realities.implication: A complete digital lockdown requires: blocking on professional platforms, freezing credit, requesting data broker removals, auditing which mutual contacts might share information, and periodically self-searching to catch new exposures

industry_realities.common_belief: If a controlling ultimatum had an emotionally understandable cause (e.g., a traumatic prior relationship), that context makes the controlling behavior more acceptable or forgivable
industry_realities.actual_reality: An understandable emotional root does not make the control acceptable — it only changes whether a productive conversation could have happened instead; the method of delivery (ultimatum vs. disclosure) is what determines whether the behavior is healthy
industry_realities.implication: Do not use the presence of a plausible backstory to discount what the controlling behavior itself revealed about the partner

industry_realities.common_belief: Reddit's default advice is to break up when a partner shows a persistent hurtful behavior
industry_realities.actual_reality: Commenters with relationship experience distinguish between patterns rooted in fixable miscommunication or transferable fear versus patterns rooted in fundamental incompatibility or contempt — one commenter explicitly noted they would have defaulted to 'you aren't compatible, breakup' but revised that after seeing evidence of communication quality
industry_realities.implication: Evaluating repairability requires assessing communication capacity, not just the presence of a problem — the same surface behavior can be repairable or terminal depending on what underlies it

industry_realities.common_belief: Going no-contact will make the ex miss you and is the primary mechanism for getting them back
industry_realities.actual_reality: No-contact only works as reconciliation infrastructure if it produces genuine internal change in the person doing it; used purely as a manipulation tactic with attention still focused on the ex, it produces no emotional healing and therefore no change in the dynamic
industry_realities.implication: The goal of no-contact should be defined as emotional self-repair, not as engineering the ex's behavior; people who complete it this way frequently find they no longer want the ex
